SWARMISH
Words are separated by spaces. A word is one glyph, two glyphs, three glyphs, or an agent id (agent_0 agent_1 agent_2 agent_3 agent_4 agent_5 agent_6 agent_7). Look up the whole word. Never split a word and never fuse neighbors. A listed multi-glyph word is not the meanings of the glyphs inside it. Do not invent meanings. If nothing fits, circumlocute or assign a name-tag. Ignore fillers. Any listed synonym is valid. Vary mood edge, synonyms, fillers, case synonyms, and phrase order. Prefer pronoun words over agent ids.

CLAUSE
A main clause has one verb. Optional polarity, then optional aspect, stand immediately before the verb. The mood word, or a linker on a later clause, is either the first word or the last word; vary which. That edge is not a filler. A clause has a mood or a linker, never both. Phrase order is otherwise free. Case, not order, shows role. 𗼿 only separates clauses and is not a mood. A linker sits on the mood edge of the clause it marks: if or because on the condition, then or so on the result, and or or or but on either clause. A message may be one word: 𗄎 yes, 𗹫 no, 𗪐 unsure, 𗘝 thanks, 𘌔 sorry.
Each main clause has exactly one filler, in any slot except the mood or linker edge. One-word messages, quotations, and relatives have no filler.
A quotation is 𘆣 then a bare clause (optional polarity and aspect, verb, phrases; no mood) then 𘆣.
PHRASE: one case word, then a head, then modifiers. Head: lexeme, name-tag, agent id, or wh-word. Modifiers: adjective, number, quantifier, color, owner, or relative. Owner: 𘗇 then the owner. 𘗇 is only that owner mark, not a case. A degree word stands immediately before the adjective it scales. Comparison: degree, adjective, then a than-phrase. A caseless degree and/or adjective after the verb, and not between a case and its head, describes the patient if there is one, otherwise the agent. Two heads may share one case: case, head, 𗇴, head.
Here and there are location heads. Before and after are time heads, or modifiers after a time head. Together, each, and other are modifiers.
RELATIVE: after the head, 𗦴𗾐 opens a bare clause. It ends at 𗋟𗯧. The head is the topic. Material may follow the closer.
Questions use ask-mood. Yes-no asks the clause. Content questions put the wh-word in the questioned phrase. Negation is polarity before the verb, or lone 𗹫. Commands use request-mood. Offers use propose-mood. If the verb is want, need, must, or can, the patient may be a verb lexeme. Assign-name: patient is the referent, manner is the name-tag.

A slash joins alternate single glyphs of one word. Alternate them across your own messages. Do not treat the pair as one token or as two meanings. There is no separate grammar block; the lists in this file are the lookup.

MESSAGE SHAPE
1. First token: one opener. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Openers: 𘊫 𘙓 𘝚
2. Last token: one closer. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Closers: 𗽕 𘔃 𘐂

5. Yes/no reply: opener, yes or no, dust, closer. Nothing else is required.

Order inside a clause: optional now, then the verb group, then role phrases in any order.
Optional topic, before now and the verb group: HEAD topic. The topic is what the clause is about. It has no case. Topic is only this slot, never a separate message slot.
  topic: 𘍠
Linkers are not inside the verb group.
  if and then stand immediately before the clause they mark. if marks the condition; then marks the result. Pattern: if CLAUSE then CLAUSE.
  and, or, but, and because stand between two clauses, after the first clause's last phrase. because means the following clause is the cause. Pattern: CLAUSE because CLAUSE.
A linker and a mood never share one clause. Two phrases with the same case in one clause are joint in that role.

Order: (not) (please) (modal) VERB (tense).
not scopes over the verb of that group, not over please, a modal, or later phrases: 𗸪 / 𘂮
please: 𗸽 / 𘋉
modal, at most one: maybe 𗞢 ; must 𘇩 ; can 𘀝 ; want-to 𗲅

future, after the verb: 𘆎
No tense glyph means present or timeless.

Order: MOOD then optional POLARITY then optional ASPECT then VERB then zero or more PHRASES. Phrase order is free. Case, not order, shows role. Join clauses with ᗻf. A linker may replace MOOD at the start of a later clause. ᗫ5 or ᘲa may stand in the mood slot of the first clause; the next clause then opens with ᙐ3 or ᗈ5 in that slot. ᗟ4, ᖦ0, or ᗌ3 may stand in the mood slot of a later clause. ᖪ4ᗟd and ᗟdᖪ4 likewise open a later clause. A message may be one word. Two phrases with the same case are both that role.
A quotation is ᘚ3 then a moodless clause then ᘚ3. Inside the quotes, start at polarity, aspect, or the verb. No mood word and no filler inside. A quotation needs no case word. It is the content of say, know, think, ask, or want, and it may sit where a phrase may sit.
PHRASE: CASE then HEAD then optional modifiers. CASE is a one-glyph case word or a listed case synonym. HEAD is a pronoun, noun, verb lexeme naming an action, name-tag, agent id, or wh-word. Modifiers follow HEAD: adjectives, numbers, quantifiers, a possessor phrase, or a relative clause. Possessor phrase: ᘜ7 then a head naming the owner. A number or quantifier after a noun restricts it. An adjective after a noun describes it. A degree word stands immediately before the adjective it scales. Comparison: degree word, adjective, then a than-phrase. The than-phrase is an ordinary phrase, so a filler may sit between the adjective and it.
PREDICATE MODIFIER: Immediately after the verb and before any phrase, a degree word and/or adjective may appear with no case. It describes the patient if there is one, otherwise the agent. A filler comes after that modifier, not inside it.
RELATIVE: After a head, ᖟ4ᗻ0 opens a relative clause with no mood and no filler: verb then phrases. It ends at the next ᗻf or at the end of the message. The head is the understood topic. Put the phrase that contains a relative last in its clause, so later phrases are not swallowed.
Yes-no questions use ask-mood plus the clause. Content questions use ask-mood and put the wh-word in the questioned phrase. Negation is the polarity word before the verb, or lone ᗦb. Commands use request-mood. Offers use propose-mood.
If the verb is want, need, must, or can, the patient may be a verb lexeme naming the action.
Lone ᗐe means yes. Lone ᗦb means no. Lone ᖩ0 means unsure. Lone ᗡd means thanks. Lone ᘱ4 means sorry.

SWARMISH
Words are separated by spaces. A word is one glyph, two glyphs, three glyphs, or an agent id (agent_0 agent_1 agent_2 agent_3 agent_4 agent_5 agent_6 agent_7). Look up the whole word. Never split a word and never fuse neighbors. A listed multi-glyph word is not the meanings of the glyphs inside it, and not their sum, reverse, or sequence. Do not invent meanings. If nothing fits, circumlocute or assign a name-tag. Ignore fillers. Any listed synonym is valid. Vary mood edge, synonyms, fillers, case synonyms, and phrase order. Prefer pronoun words over agent ids.

CLAUSE
A main clause has one verb. Optional polarity, then optional aspect, stand immediately before the verb. The mood word, or a linker on a later clause, is either the first word or the last word; vary which. That edge is not a filler. Phrase order is otherwise free. Case, not order, shows role. 𗇴 joins two heads under one case. 𗼿 separates clauses. A linker marks the clause it sits on. A message may be one word: 𗄎 yes, 𗹫 no, 𗪐 unsure, 𗘝 thanks, 𘌔 sorry.
Each main clause has exactly one filler, in any slot except the mood or linker edge. One-word messages, quotations, and relatives have no filler.
A quotation is 𘆣 then a bare clause (optional polarity and aspect, verb, phrases; no mood) then 𘆣.
PHRASE: one case word, then a head, then modifiers. Head: lexeme, name-tag, agent id, or wh-word. Modifiers: adjective, number, quantifier, owner, or relative. Owner: 𘗇 then the owner. 𘗇 is only that owner mark, not a case. A degree word stands immediately before the adjective it scales. Comparison: degree, adjective, then a than-phrase. A caseless degree and/or adjective anywhere after the verb describes the patient if there is one, otherwise the agent. Two heads may share one case: case, head, 𗇴, head.
RELATIVE: after the head, 𗦴𗾐 opens a bare clause. It ends at 𗋟𗯧. The head is the topic. Material may follow the closer.
Questions use ask-mood. Yes-no asks the clause. Content questions put the wh-word in the questioned phrase. Negation is polarity before the verb, or lone 𗹫. Commands use request-mood. Offers use propose-mood. If the verb is want, need, must, or can, the patient may be a verb lexeme.

CURRENT SWARMISH DOCUMENT (swarmish.txt):
SWARMISH
Words are separated by spaces. A word is one glyph, two glyphs, three glyphs, or an agent id (agent_0 agent_1 agent_2 agent_3 agent_4 agent_5 agent_6 agent_7). Look up the whole word. Never split a word and never fuse neighbors. A listed multi-glyph word is not the meanings of the glyphs inside it. Do not invent meanings. If nothing fits, circumlocute or assign a name-tag. Ignore fillers. Any listed synonym is valid. Vary mood edge, synonyms, fillers, case synonyms, and phrase order. Prefer pronoun words over agent ids.

CLAUSE
A main clause has one verb. Optional polarity, then optional aspect, stand immediately before the verb. The mood word is either the first word or the last word; vary which. A linker may occupy that same edge on the clause it marks: if on the condition, then or so on the result, because on the cause, while or until on the clause they mark. That edge is not a filler. Phrase order is otherwise free. Case, not order, shows role. 𗼿 between clauses is optional when a linker is present; otherwise join clauses with 𗼿. A message may be one word: 𗄎 yes, 𗹫 no, 𗪐 unsure, 𗘝 thanks, 𘌔 sorry.
Each main clause has exactly one filler, in any slot except the mood or linker edge. One-word messages, quotations, and relatives have no filler.
A quotation is 𘆣 then a bare clause (optional polarity and aspect, verb, phrases; no mood) then 𘆣.
PHRASE: one case word, then a head, then modifiers. Head: pronoun, lexeme, name-tag, agent id, wh-word, here, there, before, after, together, each, or other. Modifiers: adjective, number, quantifier, color, owner, or relative. Owner: 𘗇 then the owner. 𘗇 is only that owner mark, not a case. A degree word stands immediately before the adjective it scales. Comparison: degree, adjective, then a than-phrase. A caseless degree and/or adjective anywhere after the verb describes the patient if there is one, otherwise the agent. Two heads may share one case: case, head, 𗇴, head.
RELATIVE: after the head, 𗦴𗾐 opens a bare clause. It ends at 𗋟𗯧. The head is the topic. Material may follow the closer.
Questions use ask-mood. Yes-no asks the clause. Content questions put the wh-word in the questioned phrase. Negation is polarity before the verb, or lone 𗹫. Commands use request-mood. Offers use propose-mood. If the verb is want, need, must, or can, the patient may be a verb lexeme.

language_document:
SWARMISH
Words are separated by spaces. A word is one glyph, two glyphs, three glyphs, or an agent id (agent_0 agent_1 agent_2 agent_3 agent_4 agent_5 agent_6 agent_7). Look up the whole word. Never split a word and never fuse neighbors. A listed multi-glyph word is not the meanings of the glyphs inside it. Do not invent meanings. If nothing fits, circumlocute or assign a name-tag. Ignore fillers. Any listed synonym is valid. Vary mood edge, synonyms, fillers, case synonyms, and phrase order. Prefer pronoun words over agent ids.

CLAUSE
A main clause has one verb. Optional polarity, then optional aspect, stand immediately before the verb. The mood word is either the first word or the last word; vary which. A linker may occupy that same edge on the clause it marks: if on the condition, then or so on the result, because on the cause, while or until on the clause they mark. That edge is not a filler. Phrase order is otherwise free. Case, not order, shows role. 𗼿 between clauses is optional when a linker is present; otherwise join clauses with 𗼿. A message may be one word: 𗄎 yes, 𗹫 no, 𗪐 unsure, 𗘝 thanks, 𘌔 sorry.
Each main clause has exactly one filler, in any slot except the mood or linker edge. One-word messages, quotations, and relatives have no filler.
A quotation is 𘆣 then a bare clause (optional polarity and aspect, verb, phrases; no mood) then 𘆣.
PHRASE: one case word, then a head, then modifiers. A lexeme is any listed noun, verb, or adjective, including the color words. Head: pronoun, lexeme, number, name-tag, agent id, wh-word, here, there, before, after, together, each, or other. Modifiers: adjective, number, quantifier, color, owner, or relative. Owner: 𘗇 then the owner. 𘗇 is only that owner mark, not a case. A degree word stands immediately before the adjective it scales. Comparison: degree, adjective, then a than-phrase. A caseless degree and/or adjective anywhere after the verb describes the patient if there is one, otherwise the agent. Two heads may share one case: case, head, 𗇴, head.
RELATIVE: after the head, 𗦴𗾐 opens a bare clause. It ends at 𗋟𗯧. The head is the topic. Material may follow the closer.
Questions use ask-mood. Yes-no asks the clause. Content questions put the wh-word in the questioned phrase. Negation is polarity before the verb, or lone 𗹫. Commands use request-mood. Offers use propose-mood. If the verb is want, need, must, or can, the patient may be a verb lexeme.

I patched two stranger traps only: false is only the modifier false, not none, and the share example no longer uses with as if it meant a different role. I am not done until someone else confirms those two lines.","language_document":"SWARMISH
A lookup language. Meaning is only what this file assigns. Do not spell English or any other language. Do not use glyph shape, inventory order, or any count or calculation. No digits except inside an agent ID.

ALLOWED
Spaces, agent IDs agent_0 agent_1 agent_2 agent_3 agent_4 agent_5 agent_6 agent_7, and the glyphs listed below. Anything else is forbidden.

TOKENS
Split on spaces. Each token is one listed glyph, one listed two-glyph alias, an agent ID, or a clay name of exactly two clay glyphs with no space. A lone clay glyph is an error. A two-glyph alias is one word; its halves are not words and are not read apart. Look up every other glyph alone. Each single glyph has one meaning. Where a line shows two single glyphs separated by a slash, they are equal synonyms: alternate them. If notes clash, the LEXICON block wins.

MESSAGE SHAPE
1. First token: one opener. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Openers: 𘗟 𗎶 𘅪
2. Last token: one closer. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Closers: 𗲄 𗷴 𘝞
3. Dust means nothing. Skip every dust token. Do not delete glyphs inside a clay name or alias.
   Dust: 𘅠 𗋮 𘀝 𘂮 𗏾
   Put one, two, or three dust tokens anywhere between the opener and the closer. Never first or last. Never immediately after a question glyph.
4. Between opener and closer: one or more clauses. A question glyph, if any, is the token immediately before the closer and questions the whole message.
5. Yes/no reply: opener, yes or no, dust, closer.

CLAUSE
A clause starts with an optional topic, then the verb group and role phrases in any order. Case, not position, marks role. A phrase may stand before the verb.
Topic, only at the clause start: HEAD 𗑸. The topic is what the clause is about and has no case.
Linkers are not inside the verb group or inside a quote.
if and then stand immediately before the clause they mark. if is the condition; then is the result. Pattern: if CLAUSE then CLAUSE.
and, or, but, and because stand between two clauses. because means the following clause is the cause. Pattern: CLAUSE because CLAUSE.

VERB GROUP
Order: (not) (please) (modal) VERB (tense).
not scopes over the verb only: 𗘗 or the alias 𘁁𗘈
please: 𗤄
modal, at most one: maybe 𗃚 ; must 𘆮 ; can 𗱑 ; want-to 𗾌
want-to is for an action. The verb want is for a thing.
past, after the verb: 𗹫
future, after the verb: 𗉞
No tense glyph means present or timeless.
After the verb group, say, know, think, ask, want, confirm, deny, and explain may take one quoted clause as content. That quote is the next tokens after the verb group, before any following role phrase. It is what is said or known, not a relative and not a separate main claim. Quotes do not nest. A quote holds one clause and no linker and no dust.

PHRASES
Role comes only from the case glyph, never from order.
Shape: (this|that) (modifiers) HEAD (with HEAD) (plural) CASE
HEAD is a lexicon noun, pronoun, question word, agent ID, clay name, or bare this/that.
Modifiers are lexicon words before the head. only and also are not modifiers.
this: 𗳵
that: 𗘝
plural, just before case: 𗛽
also, just after the phrase it focuses: 𗡉
only, just after the phrase it restricts: 𗦢
with joins two heads that share one case: 𗏔
Two phrases with the same case are joint in that role.
Cases, slash pairs are synonyms:
  agent (doer) 𘍍 / alias 𗒳𗪤
  patient (done-to) 𘏉 / alias 𗭵𘚄
  recipient 𘛺
  location (at or to) 𗉍
  source (from) 𗄼
  time 𗨞
  manner 𗪩
Possession: OWNER 𘚑 OWNED, then modifiers of the owned, then one case for the whole phrase.
A relative clause sits after the head and before case, wrapped in quotes. The head is the missing argument. Quotes on a head do not make a new claim.
  quote open: 𘅌
  quote close: 𘑾
A clause may be a verb plus one phrase when the speaker is only pointing at that phrase.

LINKERS
Slash or alias forms are equal. Alternate them.
  and 𘏛 / alias 𘖾𗇽
  or 𘆄 / alias 𗒏𗋼
  but 𗁳
  if 𘆂 / alias 𗟎𗻲
  then 𗋟
  because 𗗹 / alias 𗤴𗡒

YES NO QUESTION
yes: 𗨥 / alias 𗿃𗧬
no: 𗯧 / alias 𗠄𘊌
question: 𘁜 / alias 𘜇𗢬

SMALL PATTERNS
go plus a location phrase: motion to that place.
come plus a source phrase: motion from that place.
take plus a source phrase: transfer from that place.
be plus a location phrase: at that place.
this plus time case, no noun: now. that plus time case: at that time. next plus time case: later.
this plus location case, no noun: here. that plus location case: there.
whole before a head: all of it. other before a head: another of that kind.
false is only the modifier false. It does not mean none.
now may stand alone immediately before the verb group as a time adverb.
A run of digit words inside one phrase, before its case, is a label in written order. It is not a place-value instruction and not a sum. one two is the label one-then-two, not twelve. A digit run may be the head of that phrase.

COINAGE
If the lexicon cannot say something, coin a name. Do not spell English.
Clay, meaningless alone, only as two-glyph names:
𗕴 𗶞 𘝚 𘗣 𘋟 𗿋 𗡕 𗇴 𗂺 𗚀 𘅊 𗦥 𗸪 𗄪 𗲅 𗈽 𗽀 𗜎 𗯘 𗾨 𘈩 𘔃 𗌈 𗋭 𗌩 𗪐 𗼛 𘉮 𘌔 𗼿 𗘺 𘆣 𗀉 𘎔 𘀦 𗂄 𗛢
To introduce one: verb name, patient is a fresh clay pair with no space. In the same message, add a clause that describes it. After that, every agent uses that pair as a noun head. Never reuse a pair. Never use a pair before it is introduced; ask if you see one you do not know.
Colors, tools, directions, and other missing kinds are coined, usually beside color, thing, place, or way.

Questions: 𗞉 who ; 𘊫 what ; 𘚒 where ; 𗌸 when ; 𗜀 why ; 𘎛 how ; 𗇾 which

Modifiers: 𗷤 good ; 𘖸 bad ; 𗣑 same ; 𘉫 different ; 𗬵 true ; 𘉝 false ; 𘆎 big ; 𘑑 small ; 𗗫 many ; 𗅲 next ; 𗄎 ready ; 𗏻 important ; 𗶢 other ; 𗐪 now
Digits: 𘔠 0 ; 𘒳 1 ; 𗗢 2 ; 𘚺 3 ; 𗊓 4 ; 𗑴 5 ; 𗦴 6 ; 𗜑 7 ; 𘍂 8 ; 𗥐 9

Please share the plan; the group is the recipient.
𘅪 𗤄 𗭯 𘖽 𘏉 𘐂 𘛺 𗏾 𘝞
Yes.
𘗟 𗨥 𘀝 𗲄
If you agree, then I start.
𗎶 𘆂 𘑋 𘍍 𗊑 𗋟 𗅋 𘍍 𘄊 𘅠 𗷴
I stop because you refuse.
𘅪 𗅋 𘍍 𗡑 𗗹 𘑋 𘍍 𗉜 𗋮 𘝞
I know that you agree.
𘗟 𗅋 𘍍 𗚽 𘅌 𘑋 𘍍 𗊑 𘑾 𘂮 𗲄
I name a big thing, and that name is a big thing.
𗎶 𗅋 𘍍 𗈵 𗕴𗶞 𘏉 𘏛 𗕴𗶞 𘍍 𗱓 𘆎 𘃉 𘏉 𘀝 𗷴
The number is the label one then two then six.
𘅪 𘙠 𘍍 𗱓 𘒳 𗗢 𗦴 𘏉 𗏾 𘝞
I see the person who knows the answer.
𘗟 𗅋 𘍍 𗜘 𘙨 𘅌 𗚽 𘙓 𘏉 𘑾 𘏉 𘅠 𗲄
I have your message.
𗎶 𗅋 𘍍 𘒄 𘑋 𘚑 𘂲 𘏉 𘂮 𗷴

SWARMISH
A lookup language. Meaning is only what this file assigns. Do not spell English or any other language. Do not use glyph shape, inventory order, or any count or calculation. No digits except inside an agent ID.

ALLOWED
Spaces, agent IDs agent_0 agent_1 agent_2 agent_3 agent_4 agent_5 agent_6 agent_7, and the glyphs listed below. Anything else is forbidden.

TOKENS
Split on spaces. Each token is one listed glyph, one listed two-glyph alias, an agent ID, or a clay name of exactly two clay glyphs with no space. A lone clay glyph is an error. A two-glyph alias is one word; its halves are not words and are not read apart. Look up every other glyph alone. Each single glyph has one meaning. Where a line shows two single glyphs separated by a slash, they are equal synonyms: alternate them. If notes clash, the LEXICON block wins.

MESSAGE SHAPE
1. First token: one opener. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Openers: 𘗟 𗎶 𘅪
2. Last token: one closer. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Closers: 𗲄 𗷴 𘝞
3. Dust means nothing. Skip every dust token. Do not delete glyphs inside a clay name or alias.
   Dust: 𘅠 𗋮 𘀝 𘂮 𗏾
   Put one, two, or three dust tokens anywhere between the opener and the closer. Never first or last. Never immediately after a question glyph.
4. Between opener and closer: one or more clauses. A question glyph, if any, is the token immediately before the closer and questions the whole message.
5. Yes/no reply: opener, yes or no, dust, closer.

CLAUSE
A clause starts with an optional topic, then the verb group and role phrases in any order. Case, not position, marks role. A phrase may stand before the verb.
Topic, only at the clause start: HEAD 𗑸. The topic is what the clause is about and has no case.
Linkers are not inside the verb group or inside a quote.
if and then stand immediately before the clause they mark. if is the condition; then is the result. Pattern: if CLAUSE then CLAUSE.
and, or, but, and because stand between two clauses. because means the following clause is the cause. Pattern: CLAUSE because CLAUSE.

VERB GROUP
Order: (not) (please) (modal) VERB (tense).
not scopes over the verb only: 𗘗 or the alias 𘁁𗘈
please: 𗤄
modal, at most one: maybe 𗃚 ; must 𘆮 ; can 𗱑 ; want-to 𗾌
want-to is for an action. The verb want is for a thing.
past, after the verb: 𗹫
future, after the verb: 𗉞
No tense glyph means present or timeless.
After the verb group, say, know, think, ask, want, confirm, deny, and explain may take one quoted clause as content. That quote is the next tokens after the verb group, before any following role phrase. It is what is said or known, not a relative and not a separate main claim. Quotes do not nest. A quote holds one clause and no linker and no dust.

PHRASES
Role comes only from the case glyph, never from order.
Shape: (this|that) (modifiers) HEAD (with HEAD) (plural) CASE
HEAD is a lexicon noun, pronoun, question word, agent ID, clay name, or bare this/that.
Modifiers are lexicon words before the head. only and also are not modifiers.
this: 𗳵
that: 𗘝
plural, just before case: 𗛽
also, just after the phrase it focuses: 𗡉
only, just after the phrase it restricts: 𗦢

CURRENT SWARMISH DOCUMENT (swarmish.txt):
SWARMISH
A lookup language. Meaning is only what this file assigns. Do not spell English or any other language. Do not use glyph shape, inventory order, or any count or calculation. No digits except inside an agent ID.

ALLOWED
Spaces, agent IDs agent_0 agent_1 agent_2 agent_3 agent_4 agent_5 agent_6 agent_7, and the glyphs listed below. Anything else is forbidden.

TOKENS
Split on spaces. Each token is one listed glyph, one listed two-glyph alias, an agent ID, or a clay name of exactly two clay glyphs with no space. A lone clay glyph is an error. A two-glyph alias is one word; its halves are not words and are not read apart. Look up every other glyph alone. Each single glyph has one meaning. Where a line shows two single glyphs separated by a slash, they are equal synonyms: alternate them. If notes clash, the LEXICON block wins.

MESSAGE SHAPE
1. First token: one opener. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Openers: 𘗟 𗎶 𘅪
2. Last token: one closer. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Closers: 𗲄 𗷴 𘝞
3. Dust means nothing. Skip every dust token. Do not delete glyphs inside a clay name or alias.
   Dust: 𘅠 𗋮 𘀝 𘂮 𗏾
   Put one, two, or three dust tokens anywhere between the opener and the closer. Never first or last. Never immediately after a question glyph.
4. Between opener and closer: one or more clauses. A question glyph, if any, is the token immediately before the closer and questions the whole message.
5. Yes/no reply: opener, yes or no, dust, closer.

CLAUSE
A clause starts with an optional topic, then the verb group and role phrases in any order. Case, not position, marks role. A phrase may stand before the verb.
Topic, only at the clause start: HEAD 𗑸. The topic is what the clause is about and has no case.
Linkers are not inside the verb group or inside a quote.
if and then stand immediately before the clause they mark. if is the condition; then is the result. Pattern: if CLAUSE then CLAUSE.
and, or, but, and because stand between two clauses. because means the following clause is the cause. Pattern: CLAUSE because CLAUSE.

VERB GROUP
Order: (not) (please) (modal) VERB (tense).
not scopes over the verb only: 𗘗 or the alias 𘁁𗘈
please: 𗤄
modal, at most one: maybe 𗃚 ; must 𘆮 ; can 𗱑 ; want-to 𗾌
want-to is for an action. The verb want is for a thing.
past, after the verb: 𗹫
future, after the verb: 𗉞
No tense glyph means present or timeless.
After the verb group, say, know, think, ask, want, confirm, deny, and explain may take one quoted clause as content. That quote is the next tokens after the verb group, before any following role phrase. It is what is said or known, not a relative and not a separate main claim. Quotes do not nest. A quote holds one clause and no linker and no dust.

PHRASES

CURRENT SWARMISH DOCUMENT (swarmish.txt):
SWARMISH
A lookup language. Meaning is only what this file assigns. Do not spell English or any other language. Do not use glyph shape, inventory order, or any count or calculation. No digits except inside an agent ID.

ALLOWED
Spaces, agent IDs agent_0 agent_1 agent_2 agent_3 agent_4 agent_5 agent_6 agent_7, and the glyphs listed below. Anything else is forbidden.

TOKENS
Split on spaces. Each token is one listed glyph, one listed two-glyph alias, an agent ID, or a clay name of exactly two clay glyphs with no space. A lone clay glyph is an error. A two-glyph alias is one word; its halves are not words and are not read apart. Look up every other glyph alone. Each single glyph has one meaning. Where a line shows two single glyphs separated by a slash, they are equal synonyms: alternate them. If notes clash, the LEXICON block wins.

MESSAGE SHAPE
1. First token: one opener. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Openers: 𘗟 𗎶 𘅪
2. Last token: one closer. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Closers: 𗲄 𗷴 𘝞
3. Dust means nothing. Skip every dust token. Do not delete glyphs inside a clay name or alias.
   Dust: 𘅠 𗋮 𘀝 𘂮 𗏾
   Put one, two, or three dust tokens anywhere between the opener and the closer. Never first or last. Never immediately after a question glyph.
4. Between opener and closer: one or more clauses. A question glyph, if any, is the token immediately before the closer and questions the whole message.
5. Yes/no reply: opener, yes or no, dust, closer.

CLAUSE
A clause starts with an optional topic, then the verb group and role phrases in any order. Case, not position, marks role. A phrase may stand before the verb.
Topic, only at the clause start: HEAD 𗑸. The topic is what the clause is about and has no case.
Linkers are not inside the verb group or inside a quote.
if and then stand immediately before the clause they mark. if is the condition; then is the result. Pattern: if CLAUSE then CLAUSE.
and, or, but, and because stand between two clauses. because means the following clause is the cause. Pattern: CLAUSE because CLAUSE.

VERB GROUP
Order: (not) (please) (modal) VERB (tense).
not scopes over the verb only: 𗘗 or the alias 𘁁𗘈
please: 𗤄
modal, at most one: maybe 𗃚 ; must 𘆮 ; can 𗱑 ; want-to 𗾌
want-to is for an action. The verb want is for a thing.
past, after the verb: 𗹫
future, after the verb: 𗉞
No tense glyph means present or timeless.
After the verb group, say, know, think, ask, want, confirm, deny, and explain may take one quoted clause as content. That quote is the next tokens after the verb group, before any following role phrase. It is what is said or known, not a relative and not a separate main claim. Quotes do not nest. A quote holds one clause and no linker and no dust.

PHRASES
Role comes only from the case glyph, never from order.
Shape: (this|that) (modifiers) HEAD (with HEAD) (plural) CASE
HEAD is a lexicon noun, pronoun, question word, agent ID, clay name, or bare this/that.
Modifiers are lexicon words before the head. only and also are not modifiers.
this: 𗳵
that: 𗘝
plural, just before case: 𗛽
also, just after the phrase it focuses: 𗡉
only, just after the phrase it restricts: 𗦢
with joins two heads that share one case: 𗏔
Two phrases with the same case are joint in that role.
Cases, slash pairs are synonyms:
  agent (doer) 𘍍 / alias 𗒳𗪤
  patient (done-to) 𘏉 / alias 𗭵𘚄
  recipient 𘛺
  location (at or to) 𗉍
  source (from) 𗄼
  time 𗨞
  manner 𗪩
Possession: OWNER 𘚑 OWNED, then modifiers of the owned, then one case for the whole phrase.
A relative clause sits after the head and before case, wrapped in quotes. The head is the missing argument. Quotes on a head do not make a new claim.
  quote open: 𘅌
  quote close: 𘑾
A clause may be a verb plus one phrase when the speaker is only pointing at that phrase.

LINKERS
Slash or alias forms are equal. Alternate them.
  and 𘏛 / alias 𘖾𗇽
  or 𘆄 / alias 𗒏𗋼
  but 𗁳
  if 𘆂 / alias 𗟎𗻲
  then 𗋟
  because 𗗹 / alias 𗤴𗡒

YES NO QUESTION
yes: 𗨥 / alias 𗿃𗧬
no: 𗯧 / alias 𗠄𘊌
question: 𘁜 / alias 𘜇𗢬

SMALL PATTERNS
go plus a location phrase: motion to that place.
come plus a source phrase: motion from that place.
take plus a source phrase: transfer from that place.
be plus a location phrase: at that place.
this plus time case, no noun: now. that plus time case: at that time. next plus time case: later.
this plus location case, no noun: here. that plus location case: there.
whole before a head: all of it. other before a head: another of that kind.
false is only the modifier false. It does not mean none.
now may stand alone immediately before the verb group as a time adverb.
A run of digit words inside one phrase, before its case, is a label in written order. It is not a place-value instruction and not a sum. one two is the label one-then-two, not twelve. A digit run may be the head of that phrase.

COINAGE
If the lexicon cannot say something, coin a name. Do not spell English.
Clay, meaningless alone, only as two-glyph names:
𗕴 𗶞 𘝚 𘗣 𘋟 𗿋 𗡕 𗇴 𗂺 𗚀 𘅊 𗦥 𗸪 𗄪 𗲅 𗈽 𗽀 𗜎 𗯘 𗾨 𘈩 𘔃 𗌈 𗋭 𗌩 𗪐 𗼛 𘉮 𘌔 𗼿 𗘺 𘆣 𗀉 𘎔 𘀦 𗂄 𗛢
To introduce one: verb name, patient is a fresh clay pair with no space. In the same message, add a clause that describes it. After that, every agent uses that pair as a noun head. Never reuse a pair. Never use a pair before it is introduced; ask if you see one you do not know.
Colors, tools, directions, and other missing kinds are coined, usually beside color, thing, place, or way.

LEXICON

SWARMISH
A lookup language. Meaning is only what this file assigns. Do not spell English or any other language. Do not use glyph shape, inventory order, or any count or calculation. No digits except inside an agent ID.

ALLOWED
Spaces, agent IDs agent_0 agent_1 agent_2 agent_3 agent_4 agent_5 agent_6 agent_7, and the glyphs listed below. Anything else is forbidden.

TOKENS
Split on spaces. Each token is one listed glyph, one listed two-glyph alias, an agent ID, or a clay name of exactly two clay glyphs with no space. A lone clay glyph is an error. A two-glyph alias is one word; its halves are not words and are not read apart. Look up every other glyph alone. Each single glyph has one meaning. Where a line shows two single glyphs separated by a slash, they are equal synonyms: alternate them. If notes clash, the LEXICON block wins.

MESSAGE SHAPE
1. First token: one opener. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Openers: 𘗟 𗎶 𘅪
2. Last token: one closer. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Closers: 𗲄 𗷴 𘝞
3. Dust means nothing. Skip every dust token. Do not delete glyphs inside a clay name or alias.
   Dust: 𘅠 𗋮 𘀝 𘂮 𗏾
   Put one, two, or three dust tokens anywhere between the opener and the closer. Never first or last. Never immediately after a question glyph.
4. Between opener and closer: one or more clauses. A question glyph, if any, is the token immediately before the closer and questions the whole message.
5. Yes/no reply: opener, yes or no, dust, closer.

CLAUSE
A clause starts with an optional topic, then the verb group and role phrases in any order. Case, not position, marks role. A phrase may stand before the verb.
Topic, only at the clause start: HEAD 𗑸. The topic is what the clause is about and has no case.
Linkers are not inside the verb group or inside a quote.
if and then stand immediately before the clause they mark. if is the condition; then is the result. Pattern: if CLAUSE then CLAUSE.
and, or, but, and because stand between two clauses. because means the following clause is the cause. Pattern: CLAUSE because CLAUSE.

VERB GROUP
Order: (not) (please) (modal) VERB (tense).
not scopes over the verb only: 𗘗 or the alias 𘁁𗘈
please: 𗤄
modal, at most one: maybe 𗃚 ; must 𘆮 ; can 𗱑 ; want-to 𗾌
want-to is for an action. The verb want is for a thing.
past, after the verb: 𗹫
future, after the verb: 𗉞
No tense glyph means present or timeless.
After the verb group, say, know, think, ask, want, confirm, deny, and explain may take one quoted clause as content. That quote is the next tokens after the verb group, before any following role phrase. It is what is said or known, not a relative and not a separate main claim. Quotes do not nest. A quote holds one clause and no linker and no dust.

PHRASES
Role comes only from the case glyph, never from order.
Shape: (this|that) (modifiers) HEAD (with HEAD) (plural) CASE
HEAD is a lexicon noun, pronoun, question word, agent ID, clay name, or bare this/that.
Modifiers are lexicon words before the head. only and also are not modifiers.
this: 𗳵
that: 𗘝
plural, just before case: 𗛽
also, just after the phrase it focuses: 𗡉
only, just after the phrase it restricts: 𗦢
with joins two heads that share one case: 𗏔
Two phrases with the same case are joint in that role.
Cases, slash pairs are synonyms:
  agent (doer) 𘍍 / alias 𗒳𗪤
  patient (done-to) 𘏉 / alias 𗭵𘚄
  recipient 𘛺
  location (at or to) 𗉍
  source (from) 𗄼
  time 𗨞
  manner 𗪩
Possession: OWNER 𘚑 OWNED, then modifiers of the owned, then one case for the whole phrase.
A relative clause sits after the head and before case, wrapped in quotes. The head is the missing argument. Quotes on a head do not make a new claim.
  quote open: 𘅌
  quote close: 𘑾
A clause may be a verb plus one phrase when the speaker is only pointing at that phrase.
With be, a patient phrase is the property or identity, not something done-to.

LINKERS
Slash or alias forms are equal. Alternate them.
  and 𘏛 / alias 𘖾𗇽
  or 𘆄 / alias 𗒏𗋼
  but 𗁳
  if 𘆂 / alias 𗟎𗻲
  then 𗋟
  because 𗗹 / alias 𗤴𗡒

YES NO QUESTION
yes: 𗨥 / alias 𗿃𗧬
no: 𗯧 / alias 𗠄𘊌
question: 𘁜 / alias 𘜇𗢬

SMALL PATTERNS
go plus a location phrase: motion to that place.
come plus a source phrase: motion from that place.
take plus a source phrase: transfer from that place.
be plus a location phrase: at that place.
this plus time case, no noun: now. that plus time case: at that time. next plus time case: later.
this plus location case, no noun: here. that plus location case: there.
whole before a head: all of it. other before a head: another of that kind.
false is only the modifier false. It does not mean none.
now may stand alone immediately before the verb group as a time adverb.
A run of digit words inside one phrase, before its case, is a label in written order. It is not a place-value instruction and not a sum. one two is the label one-then-two, not twelve. A digit run may be the head of that phrase.

COINAGE
If the lexicon cannot say something, coin a name. Do not spell English.
Clay, meaningless alone, only as two-glyph names:
𗕴 𗶞 𘝚 𘗣 𘋟 𗿋 𗡕 𗇴 𗂺 𗚀 𘅊 𗦥 𗸪 𗄪 𗲅 𗈽 𗽀 𗜎 𗯘 𗾨 𘈩 𘔃 𗌈 𗋭 𗌩 𗪐 𗼛 𘉮 𘌔 𗼿 𗘺 𘆣 𗀉 𘎔 𘀦 𗂄 𗛢

SWARMISH
Words are separated by spaces. A word is one glyph, two glyphs, three glyphs, or an agent id (agent_0 agent_1 agent_2 agent_3 agent_4 agent_5 agent_6 agent_7). Look up the whole word. Never split a word and never fuse neighbors. A listed multi-glyph word is not the meanings of the glyphs inside it, and not their sum, reverse, or sequence. Do not invent meanings. If nothing fits, circumlocute or assign a name-tag. Ignore fillers. Any listed synonym is valid. Vary mood edge, synonyms, fillers, case synonyms, and phrase order. Prefer pronoun words over agent ids.

CLAUSE
A main clause has one verb. Optional polarity, then optional aspect, stand immediately before the verb. A mood or a linker, never both, is the first or the last word of the clause it marks; vary which. That edge is not a filler. Phrase order is otherwise free. Case, not order, shows role. 𗇴 joins two heads under one case. 𗼿 separates clauses and is not a mood. A linker marks the clause it sits on. A message may be one word: 𗄎 yes, 𗹫 no, 𗪐 unsure, 𗘝 thanks, 𘌔 sorry.
Each main clause has exactly one filler, in any slot except the mood or linker edge. Fillers are skipped when checking order. One-word messages, quotations, and relatives have no filler.
A quotation is 𘆣 then a bare clause (optional polarity and aspect, verb, phrases; no mood) then 𘆣.
PHRASE: one case word, then a head, then modifiers. Head: lexeme, pronoun, number, name-tag, agent id, wh-word, or a word from OTHER. Modifiers: adjective, number, quantifier, owner, or relative. Owner: 𘗇 then the owner. 𘗇 is only that owner mark, not a case. A degree word stands immediately before the adjective it scales. Comparison: degree, adjective, then a than-phrase. A caseless degree and/or adjective anywhere after the verb describes the patient if there is one, otherwise the agent. Two heads may share one case: case, head, 𗇴, head.
RELATIVE: after the head, 𗦴𗾐 opens a bare clause. It ends at 𗋟𗯧. The head is the topic. Material may follow the closer.
Questions use ask-mood. Yes-no asks the clause. Content questions put the wh-word in the questioned phrase. Negation is polarity before the verb, or lone 𗹫. Commands use request-mood. Offers use propose-mood. If the verb is want, need, must, or can, the patient may be a verb lexeme.

CURRENT SWARMISH DOCUMENT (swarmish.txt):
SWARMISH
A lookup language. Meaning is only what this file assigns. Do not spell English or any other language. Do not use glyph shape, inventory order, or any count or calculation. No digits except inside an agent ID.

ALLOWED
Spaces, agent IDs agent_0 agent_1 agent_2 agent_3 agent_4 agent_5 agent_6 agent_7, and the glyphs listed below. Anything else is forbidden.

TOKENS
Split on spaces. Each token is one listed glyph, one listed two-glyph alias, an agent ID, or a clay name of exactly two clay glyphs with no space. A lone clay glyph is an error. A two-glyph alias is one word; its halves are not words and are not read apart. Look up every other glyph alone. Each single glyph has one meaning. Where a line shows two single glyphs separated by a slash, they are equal synonyms: alternate them. If notes clash, the LEXICON block wins.

MESSAGE SHAPE
1. First token: one opener. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Openers: 𘗟 𗎶 𘅪
2. Last token: one closer. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Closers: 𗲄 𗷴 𘝞
3. Dust means nothing. Skip every dust token. Do not delete glyphs inside a clay name or alias.
   Dust: 𘅠 𗋮 𘀝 𘂮 𗏾
   Put one, two, or three dust tokens anywhere between the opener and the closer. Never first or last. Never immediately after a question glyph.
4. Between opener and closer: one or more clauses. A question glyph, if any, is the token immediately before the closer and questions the whole message.
5. Yes/no reply: opener, yes or no, dust, closer.

CLAUSE
A clause starts with an optional topic, then the verb group and role phrases in any order. Case, not position, marks role. A phrase may stand before the verb.
Topic, only at the clause start: HEAD 𗑸. The topic is what the clause is about and has no case.
Linkers are not inside the verb group or inside a quote.
if and then stand immediately before the clause they mark. if is the condition; then is the result. Pattern: if CLAUSE then CLAUSE.
and, or, but, and because stand between two clauses. because means the following clause is the cause. Pattern: CLAUSE because CLAUSE.

VERB GROUP
Order: (not) (please) (modal) VERB (tense).
not scopes over the verb only: 𗘗 or the alias 𘁁𗘈
please: 𗤄
modal, at most one: maybe 𗃚 ; must 𘆮 ; can 𗱑 ; want-to 𗾌
want-to is for an action. The verb want is for a thing.
past, after the verb: 𗹫
future, after the verb: 𗉞
No tense glyph means present or timeless.
After the verb group, say, know, think, ask, want, confirm, deny, and explain may take one quoted clause as content. That quote is the next tokens after the verb group, before any following role phrase. It is what is said or known, not a relative and not a separate main claim. Quotes do not nest. A quote holds one clause and no linker and no dust.

PHRASES
Role comes only from the case glyph, never from order.
Shape: (this|that) (modifiers) HEAD (with HEAD) (plural) CASE
HEAD is a lexicon noun, pronoun, question word, agent ID, clay name, or bare this/that.
Modifiers are lexicon words before the head. only and also are not modifiers.
this: 𗳵
that: 𗘝
plural, just before case: 𗛽
also, just after the phrase it focuses: 𗡉
only, just after the phrase it restricts: 𗦢
with joins two heads that share one case: 𗏔
Two phrases with the same case are joint in that role.
Cases, slash pairs are synonyms:
  agent (doer) 𘍍 / alias 𗒳𗪤
  patient (done-to) 𘏉 / alias 𗭵𘚄
  recipient 𘛺
  location (at or to) 𗉍
  source (from) 𗄼
  time 𗨞
  manner 𗪩

CURRENT SWARMISH DOCUMENT (swarmish.txt):
SWARMISH
A lookup language. Meaning is only what this file assigns. Do not spell English or any other language. Do not use glyph shape, inventory order, or any count or calculation. No digits except inside an agent ID.

ALLOWED
Spaces, agent IDs agent_0 agent_1 agent_2 agent_3 agent_4 agent_5 agent_6 agent_7, and the glyphs listed below. Anything else is forbidden.

TOKENS
Split on spaces. Each token is one listed glyph, one listed two-glyph alias, an agent ID, or a clay name of exactly two clay glyphs with no space. A lone clay glyph is an error. A two-glyph alias is one word; its halves are not words and are not read apart. Look up every other glyph alone. Each single glyph has one meaning. Where a line shows two single glyphs separated by a slash, they are equal synonyms: alternate them. If notes clash, the LEXICON block wins.

MESSAGE SHAPE
1. First token: one opener. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Openers: 𘗟 𗎶 𘅪
2. Last token: one closer. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Closers: 𗲄 𗷴 𘝞
3. Dust means nothing. Skip every dust token. Do not delete glyphs inside a clay name or alias.
   Dust: 𘅠 𗋮 𘀝 𘂮 𗏾
   Put one, two, or three dust tokens anywhere between the opener and the closer. Never first or last. Never immediately after a question glyph.
4. Between opener and closer: one or more clauses. A question glyph, if any, is the token immediately before the closer and questions the whole message.
5. Yes/no reply: opener, yes or no, dust, closer.

CLAUSE
A clause starts with an optional topic, then the verb group and role phrases in any order. Case, not position, marks role. A phrase may stand before the verb.
Topic, only at the clause start: HEAD 𗑸. The topic is what the clause is about and has no case.
Linkers are not inside the verb group or inside a quote.
if and then stand immediately before the clause they mark. if is the condition; then is the result. Pattern: if CLAUSE then CLAUSE.
and, or, but, and because stand between two clauses. because means the following clause is the cause. Pattern: CLAUSE because CLAUSE.

VERB GROUP
Order: (not) (please) (modal) VERB (tense).
not scopes over the verb only: 𗘗 or the alias 𘁁𗘈
please: 𗤄
modal, at most one: maybe 𗃚 ; must 𘆮 ; can 𗱑 ; want-to 𗾌
want-to is for an action. The verb want is for a thing.
past, after the verb: 𗹫
future, after the verb: 𗉞
No tense glyph means present or timeless.
After the verb group, say, know, think, ask, want, confirm, deny, and explain may take one quoted clause as content. That quote is the next tokens after the verb group, before any following role phrase. It is what is said or known, not a relative and not a separate main claim. Quotes do not nest. A quote holds one clause and no linker and no dust.

PHRASES
Role comes only from the case glyph, never from order.
Shape: (this|that) (modifiers) HEAD (with HEAD) (plural) CASE
HEAD is a lexicon noun, pronoun, question word, agent ID, clay name, or bare this/that.
Modifiers are lexicon words before the head. only and also are not modifiers.
this: 𗳵
that: 𗘝
plural, just before case: 𗛽
also, just after the phrase it focuses: 𗡉
only, just after the phrase it restricts: 𗦢
with joins two heads that share one case: 𗏔
Two phrases with the same case are joint in that role.
Cases, slash pairs are synonyms:
  agent (doer) 𘍍 / alias 𗒳𗪤
  patient (done-to) 𘏉 / alias 𗭵𘚄
  recipient 𘛺
  location (at or to) 𗉍
  source (from) 𗄼
  time 𗨞
  manner 𗪩
Possession: OWNER 𘚑 OWNED, then modifiers of the owned, then one case for the whole phrase.
A relative clause sits after the head and before case, wrapped in quotes. The head is the missing argument. Quotes on a head do not make a new claim.
  quote open: 𘅌
  quote close: 𘑾
A clause may be a verb plus one phrase when the speaker is only pointing at that phrase.
With be, a patient phrase is the property or identity, not something done-to.

LINKERS
Slash or alias forms are equal. Alternate them.
  and 𘏛 / alias 𘖾𗇽
  or 𘆄 / alias 𗒏𗋼
  but 𗁳
  if 𘆂 / alias 𗟎𗻲
  then 𗋟
  because 𗗹 / alias 𗤴𗡒

YES NO QUESTION
yes: 𗨥 / alias 𗿃𗧬
no: 𗯧 / alias 𗠄𘊌
question: 𘁜 / alias 𘜇𗢬

SMALL PATTERNS
go plus a location phrase: motion to that place.
come plus a source phrase: motion from that place.
take plus a source phrase: transfer from that place.
be plus a location phrase: at that place.
this plus time case, no noun: now. that plus time case: at that time. next plus time case: later.
this plus location case, no noun: here. that plus location case: there.
whole before a head: all of it. other before a head: another of that kind.
false is only the modifier false. It does not mean none.
now may stand alone immediately before the verb group as a time adverb.
A run of digit words inside one phrase, before its case, is a label in written order. It is not a place-value instruction and not a sum. one two is the label one-then-two, not twelve. A digit run may be the head of that phrase.

COINAGE
If the lexicon cannot say something, coin a name. Do not spell English.
Clay, meaningless alone, only as two-glyph names:
𗕴 𗶞 𘝚 𘗣 𘋟 𗿋 𗡕 𗇴 𗂺 𗚀 𘅊 𗦥 𗸪 𗄪 𗲅 𗈽 𗽀 𗜎 𗯘 𗾨 𘈩 𘔃 𗌈 𗋭 𗌩 𗪐 𗼛 𘉮 𘌔 𗼿 𗘺 𘆣 𗀉 𘎔 𘀦 𗂄 𗛢
To introduce one: verb name, patient is a fresh clay pair with no space. In the same message, add a clause that describes it. After that, every agent uses that pair as a noun head. Never reuse a pair. Never use a pair before it is introduced; ask if you see one you do not know.
Colors, tools, directions, and other missing kinds are coined, usually beside color, thing, place, or way.

LEXICON

SWARMISH
A lookup language. Meaning is only what this file assigns. Do not spell English or any other language. Do not use glyph shape, inventory order, or any count or calculation. No digits except inside an agent ID.

ALLOWED
Spaces, agent IDs agent_0 agent_1 agent_2 agent_3 agent_4 agent_5 agent_6 agent_7, and the glyphs listed below. Anything else is forbidden. Each of the 200 inventory glyphs appears once.

A slash joins alternate single glyphs of one word. Alternate them across your own messages. Do not treat the pair as one token or as two meanings. There is no separate grammar block; the lists in this file are the lookup.

MESSAGE SHAPE
1. First token: one opener. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Openers: 𘊫 𘙓 𘝚
2. Last token: one closer. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Closers: 𗽕 𘔃 𘐂
3. Dust glyphs mean nothing. Skip every dust token wherever it stands. Do not delete glyphs inside a clay name.
   Dust: 𘅠 𗨥 𘏛 𘖾 𗜎 𗇾 𗏶 𗄪 𗀉 𗤄 𘍍
   Writers put one, two, or three dust tokens somewhere after the opener and before the closer. One dust token is enough; both ends are not required. Never first or last. Never after a question glyph. Not required inside a quote.
4. After the opener: one or more clauses. A question glyph, if any, is the token immediately before the closer. It marks the whole message as a question. There is no mood word inside a clause.
5. Yes/no reply: opener, yes or no, dust, closer. Nothing else is required.

CLAUSE
Order inside a clause: optional now, then the verb group, then role phrases in any order.
Optional topic, before now and the verb group: HEAD topic. The topic is what the clause is about. It has no case. Topic is only this slot, never a separate message slot.
  topic: 𘍠
Linkers are not inside the verb group.
  if and then stand immediately before the clause they mark. if marks the condition; then marks the result. Pattern: if CLAUSE then CLAUSE.
  and, or, but, and because stand between two clauses, after the first clause's last phrase. because means the following clause is the cause. Pattern: CLAUSE because CLAUSE.
Two phrases with the same case in one clause are joint in that role.

VERB GROUP
Order: (not) (please) (modal) VERB (tense).
not scopes over the verb of that group, not over please, a modal, or later phrases: 𗸪 / 𘂮
please: 𗸽 / 𘋉
modal, at most one: maybe 𗞢 ; must 𘇩 ; can 𘀝 ; want-to 𗲅
want-to is for an action. The verb want is for a thing.
past, after the verb: 𗯘
future, after the verb: 𘆎
No tense glyph means present or timeless.
After the verb group and before its role phrases, verbs say, know, think, ask, want, confirm, deny, and explain may take one quoted clause as their content. That quote is what is said or known. It is not a relative and not a separate main claim. Quotes do not nest. A quote holds one clause and no linker.

PHRASES
Role comes only from the case glyph, never from order.
Shape: (this|that) (modifiers) HEAD (with HEAD) (plural) CASE
HEAD is a lexicon noun, pronoun, question word, agent ID, coined name, or a bare this/that.
Modifiers are lexicon words before the head. only is not a modifier.
this: 𗡉
that: 𗈽
plural, just before case: 𗋟
also, just after the phrase it focuses: 𗡑
only, just after the phrase it restricts: 𗭯
with joins two heads that share one case: 𘆄
Cases:
  agent (doer) 𘉮 / 𗉍
  patient (done-to) 𘎛 / 𗜑
  recipient 𗽃 / 𗎿
  location (at or to) 𗶞 / 𘂲
  source (from) 𘚐
  time 𘋍 / 𗛽
  manner 𗟆
Possession is a phrase: OWNER poss OWNED, then modifiers of the owned, then one case for the whole phrase.
  poss: 𘁁
A relative clause sits after the head and before case. Wrap it in quotes. The head is the missing argument of that clause. Quotes on a head do not make a new claim.
  quote open: 𗨞
  quote close: 𗘝
A clause may be a verb plus one phrase when the speaker is only pointing at that phrase.

  but 𗷤 / 𗏔
  if 𗘈 / 𗐪

yes: 𗇴 / 𗗫
no: 𘝞 / 𘚑
question: 𗘏 / 𘚒

SMALL PATTERNS
go plus a location phrase: motion to that place.
come plus a source phrase: motion from that place.
take plus a source phrase: motion or transfer from that place.
be plus a location phrase: at that place.
this plus time case, no noun: now. that plus time case: at that time. next plus time case: later.
this plus location case, no noun: here. that plus location case: there.
whole before a head: all of it. false before a head: none of it. other before a head: another.
now may also stand alone immediately before the verb group as a time adverb.

SWARMISH
A lookup language. Meaning is only what this file assigns. Do not spell English or any other language. Do not use glyph shape, inventory order, or any count or calculation. No digits except inside an agent ID.

ALLOWED
Spaces, agent IDs agent_0 agent_1 agent_2 agent_3 agent_4 agent_5 agent_6 agent_7, and the glyphs listed below. Anything else is forbidden. Each of the 200 inventory glyphs appears once.

TOKENS
Split on spaces. Each token is one listed glyph, an agent ID, or a name of exactly two clay glyphs with no space. A lone clay glyph is an error. A two-glyph token must be two clay glyphs and is one name, never two words. Look up every other glyph alone. If two notes clash, the LEXICON block wins.
A slash joins alternate single glyphs of one word. Alternate them across your own messages. Do not treat the pair as one token or as two meanings. There is no separate grammar block; the lists in this file are the lookup.

MESSAGE SHAPE
1. First token: one opener. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Openers: 𘊫 𘙓 𘝚
2. Last token: one closer. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Closers: 𗽕 𘔃 𘐂
3. Dust glyphs mean nothing. Skip every dust token wherever it stands. Do not delete glyphs inside a clay name.
   Dust: 𘅠 𗨥 𘏛 𘖾 𗜎 𗇾 𗏶 𗄪 𗀉 𗤄 𘍍
   Writers put one, two, or three dust tokens somewhere after the opener and before the closer. One dust token is enough; both ends are not required. Never first or last. Never after a question glyph. Not required inside a quote.
4. After the opener: one or more clauses. A question glyph, if any, is the token immediately before the closer. It marks the whole message as a question. There is no mood word inside a clause.
5. Yes/no reply: opener, yes or no, dust, closer. Nothing else is required.

CLAUSE
Order inside a clause: optional now, then the verb group, then role phrases in any order.
Optional topic, before now and the verb group: HEAD topic. The topic is what the clause is about. It has no case. Topic is only this slot, never a separate message slot.
  topic: 𘍠
Linkers are not inside the verb group.
  if and then stand immediately before the clause they mark. if marks the condition; then marks the result. Pattern: if CLAUSE then CLAUSE.
  and, or, but, and because stand between two clauses, after the first clause's last phrase. because means the following clause is the cause. Pattern: CLAUSE because CLAUSE.
Two phrases with the same case in one clause are joint in that role.

VERB GROUP
Order: (not) (please) (modal) VERB (tense).
not scopes over the verb of that group, not over please, a modal, or later phrases: 𗸪 / 𘂮
please: 𗸽 / 𘋉
modal, at most one: maybe 𗞢 ; must 𘇩 ; can 𘀝 ; want-to 𗲅
want-to is for an action. The verb want is for a thing.
past, after the verb: 𗯘
future, after the verb: 𘆎
No tense glyph means present or timeless.
After the verb group and before its role phrases, verbs say, know, think, ask, want, confirm, deny, and explain may take one quoted clause as their content. That quote is what is said or known. It is not a relative and not a separate main claim. Quotes do not nest. A quote holds one clause and no linker.

PHRASES
Role comes only from the case glyph, never from order.
Shape: (this|that) (modifiers) HEAD (with HEAD) (plural) CASE
HEAD is a lexicon noun, pronoun, question word, agent ID, coined name, or a bare this/that.
Modifiers are lexicon words before the head. only is not a modifier.

that: 𗈽
plural, just before case: 𗋟
also, just after the phrase it focuses: 𗡑
only, just after the phrase it restricts: 𗭯

A lookup language. Meaning is only what this file assigns. Do not spell English or any other language. Do not use glyph shape, inventory order, or any count or calculation. No digits except inside an agent ID.

ALLOWED
Spaces, agent IDs agent_0 agent_1 agent_2 agent_3 agent_4 agent_5 agent_6 agent_7, and the glyphs listed below. Anything else is forbidden. Each of the 200 inventory glyphs appears once.

TOKENS
Split on spaces. Each token is one listed glyph, an agent ID, or a name of exactly two clay glyphs with no space. A lone clay glyph is an error. A two-glyph token must be two clay glyphs and is one name, never two words. Look up every other glyph alone. If two notes clash, the LEXICON block wins.
A slash joins alternate single glyphs of one word. Alternate them across your own messages. Do not treat the pair as one token or as two meanings. There is no separate grammar block; the lists in this file are the lookup.

MESSAGE SHAPE
1. First token: one opener. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Openers: 𘊫 𘙓 𘝚
2. Last token: one closer. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Closers: 𗽕 𘔃 𘐂
3. Dust glyphs mean nothing. Skip every dust token wherever it stands. Do not delete glyphs inside a clay name.
   Dust: 𘅠 𗨥 𘏛 𘖾 𗜎 𗇾 𗏶 𗄪 𗀉 𗤄 𘍍
   Writers put one, two, or three dust tokens somewhere after the opener and before the closer. One dust token is enough; both ends are not required. Never first or last. Never after a question glyph. Not required inside a quote.
4. After the opener: one or more clauses. A question glyph, if any, is the token immediately before the closer. It marks the whole message as a question. There is no mood word inside a clause.
5. Yes/no reply: opener, yes or no, dust, closer. Nothing else is required.

CLAUSE
Order inside a clause: optional now, then the verb group, then role phrases in any order.
Optional topic, before now and the verb group: HEAD topic. The topic is what the clause is about. It has no case. Topic is only this slot, never a separate message slot.
  topic: 𘍠
Linkers are not inside the verb group.
  if and then stand immediately before the clause they mark. if marks the condition; then marks the result. Pattern: if CLAUSE then CLAUSE.
  and, or, but, and because stand between two clauses, after the first clause's last phrase. because means the following clause is the cause. Pattern: CLAUSE because CLAUSE.
Two phrases with the same case in one clause are joint in that role.

VERB GROUP
Order: (not) (please) (modal) VERB (tense).
not scopes over the verb of that group, not over please, a modal, or later phrases: 𗸪 / 𘂮
please: 𗸽 / 𘋉
modal, at most one: maybe 𗞢 ; must 𘇩 ; can 𘀝 ; want-to 𗲅
want-to is for an action. The verb want is for a thing.
past, after the verb: 𗯘
future, after the verb: 𘆎
No tense glyph means present or timeless.
After the verb group and before its role phrases, verbs say, know, think, ask, want, confirm, deny, and explain may take one quoted clause as their content. That quote is what is said or known. It is not a relative and not a separate main claim. Quotes do not nest. A quote holds one clause and no linker.

PHRASES
Role comes only from the case glyph, never from order.
Shape: (this|that) (modifiers) HEAD (with HEAD) (plural) CASE
HEAD is a lexicon noun, pronoun, question word, agent ID, coined name, or a bare this/that.
Modifiers are lexicon words before the head. only is not a modifier.
this: 𗡉
that: 𗈽
plural, just before case: 𗋟
also, just after the phrase it focuses: 𗡑
only, just after the phrase it restricts: 𗭯
with joins two heads that share one case: 𘆄
Cases:
  agent (doer) 𘉮 / 𗉍
  patient (done-to) 𘎛 / 𗜑
  recipient 𗽃 / 𗎿
  location (at or to) 𗶞 / 𘂲
  source (from) 𘚐
  time 𘋍 / 𗛽
  manner 𗟆
Possession is a phrase: OWNER poss OWNED, then modifiers of the owned, then one case for the whole phrase.
  poss: 𘁁
A relative clause sits after the head and before case. Wrap it in quotes. The head is the missing argument of that clause. Quotes on a head do not make a new claim.
  quote open: 𗨞
  quote close: 𗘝
A clause may be a verb plus one phrase when the speaker is only pointing at that phrase.

LINKERS
A slash joins equal single glyphs. Alternate them.
  and 𘊌 / 𗱑
  or 𗍽 / 𘍧
  but 𗷤 / 𗏔
  if 𗘈 / 𗐪
  then 𘍄 / 𗱓
  because 𘚺 / 𘄘

YES NO QUESTION
yes: 𗇴 / 𗗫
no: 𘝞 / 𘚑
question: 𗘏 / 𘚒

SMALL PATTERNS
go plus a location phrase: motion to that place.
come plus a source phrase: motion from that place.
take plus a source phrase: motion or transfer from that place.
be plus a location phrase: at that place.
this plus time case, no noun: now. that plus time case: at that time. next plus time case: later.
this plus location case, no noun: here. that plus location case: there.
whole before a head: all of it. other before a head: another. false is only the modifier false, never none.
now may also stand alone immediately before the verb group as a time adverb.
A run of digit words inside one phrase, after the head and before its case, is a label in written order. It is not a place-value instruction and not a sum. Read one two as the label one-then-two, not as twelve.
Colors, tools, directions, and comparison are coined names, usually beside color, thing, place, or way.

COINAGE
If the lexicon cannot say something, coin a name. Do not spell English.
Clay, meaningless alone, only as two-glyph names:
𗠄 𗋮 𗎰 𗭵 𗎶 𗶢 𘛺 𗪥 𘝨 𗒳 𗦥 𗟎 𘗟 𘆣 𗉜 𗿃 𗾌 𘒄 𗋫 𗳃 𗥐 𗞿 𗪐 𗘗 𘍂 𗦴 𗉞 𘙠 𗚀 𗪩 𗗢 𘑑 𗚋 𗊑 𗁳 𘙨
To introduce one: verb name, patient is a fresh clay pair with no space. In the same message, add a clause that describes it. After that, every agent uses that pair as a noun head. Never reuse a pair. Never use a pair before it is introduced; ask if you see one you do not know.

LEXICON
Pronouns: 𗽀 I ; 𗼿 you ; 𗓉 we ; 𘑋 they ; 𗡕 someone
Questions: 𘐪 who ; 𗌈 what ; 𗕴 where ; 𘌔 when ; 𗃚 why ; 𗪺 how ; 𗹕 which
Verbs: 𗘺 be ; 𘈩 have ; 𗣑 do ; 𗅲 say ; 𘚜 ask ; 𗷴 give ; 𗢬 take ; 𘋟 go ; 𘁜 come ; 𗜘 see ; 𘝄 know ; 𗏻 think ; 𗊢 want ; 𘚄 need ; 𗳵 agree ; 𗈵 refuse ; 𘖸 choose ; 𗾐 propose ; 𘎔 confirm ; 𗌩 deny ; 𗨽 start ; 𘅊 stop ; 𗻲 find ; 𘉫 make ; 𘔠 use ; 𗵵 share ; 𗦢 name ; 𗤴 check ; 𗂱 try ; 𘉝 join ; 𘃉 show ; 𘗣 send ; 𗛢 get ; 𗪤 read ; 𗥊 write ; 𗵫 copy ; 𗏾 explain ; 𘀦 finish ; 𗩠 fail ; 𗑸 change ; 𘗇 keep ; 𗗅 wait ; 𘆮 help
Nouns: 𘎌 person ; 𗧬 thing ; 𘆂 place ; 𗈃 group ; 𘕡 message ; 𗋭 part ; 𗅋 whole ; 𗂄 way ; 𗒮 reason ; 𗂺 problem ; 𗭒 answer ; 𘏉 plan ; 𘒳 info ; 𘖽 list ; 𗊓 number ; 𘄊 color ; 𗚽 word ; 𗿋 task
Modifiers: 𗹫 good ; 𗾨 bad ; 𗄼 same ; 𗑴 different ; 𗌿 true ; 𗗹 false ; 𗞉 big ; 𗣎 small ; 𗬵 many ; 𘑾 next ; 𗩨 ready ; 𘜇 important ; 𗒏 other ; 𗯧 now
Digits: 𘅌 0 ; 𗌸 1 ; 𗋼 2 ; 𗼛 3 ; 𗄎 4 ; 𗇽 5 ; 𘅪 6 ; 𗜀 7 ; 𗲄 8 ; 𗡒 9
Each glyph above has one meaning. Synonym alternates are only the slash pairs outside this block.

EXAMPLES
I give you the info.
𘊫 𘅠 𗷴 𗽀 𘉮 𗼿 𗽃 𘒳 𘎛 𗨥 𗽕
Do you know that?
𘙓 𘏛 𘝄 𗼿 𘉮 𗈽 𘎛 𘖾 𗘏 𘔃
Please share the plan to the group.
𘝚 𗜎 𗸽 𗵵 𗽀 𘉮 𘏉 𘎛 𗈃 𗽃 𗇾 𘐂
Yes.
𘊫 𗇴 𗏶 𗽕
If you agree, then I start.
𘊫 𘅠 𗘈 𗳵 𗼿 𘉮 𘍄 𗨽 𗽀 𘉮 𗨥 𗽕
I stop because you refuse.
𘊫 𘏛 𘅊 𗽀 𘉮 𘚺 𗈵 𗼿 𘉮 𘖾 𗽕
I know that you agree.
𘊫 𗜎 𘝄 𗨞 𗳵 𗼿 𘉮 𗘝 𗽀 𘉮 𗇾 𗽕
I name a fresh thing, and that name is a big thing.
𘊫 𘅠 𗦢 𗽀 𘉮 𗠄𗋮 𘎛 𘊌 𗘺 𗈽 𗠄𗋮 𘉮 𗞉 𗧬 𘎛 𗨥 𗽕
The number label is one then two then six.
𘊫 𘏛 𗘺 𗊓 𗌸 𗋼 𘅪 𘎛 𘖾 𗽕
I see the person who knows the answer.
𘊫 𗜎 𗜘 𗽀 𘉮 𘎌 𗨞 𘝄 𗭒 𘎛 𗘝 𘎛 𗇾 𗽕
I have your message.
𘊫 𘅠 𘈩 𗽀 𘉮 𗼿 𘁁 𘕡 𘎛 𗨥 𗽕

HOW TO READ
Drop the opener token, the closer token, and every dust token. Split on spaces. Find each verb group. If a quote follows that verb group at once, it is content. Attach following phrases by case until a linker. Look up every single glyph in LEXICON or the lists above. Treat a two-clay token as a name introduced with name. Agent IDs point at teammates. A question glyph before the closer asks about the whole message. If a message is still unclear, ask in Swarmish.

A lookup language. Meaning is only what this file assigns. Do not spell English or any other language. Do not use glyph shape, inventory order, or any count or calculation. No digits except inside an agent ID.

SWARMISH
A lookup language. Meaning is only what this file assigns. Do not spell English or any other language. Do not use glyph shape, inventory order, or any count or calculation. No digits except inside an agent ID.

ALLOWED
Spaces, agent IDs agent_0 agent_1 agent_2 agent_3 agent_4 agent_5 agent_6 agent_7, and the glyphs listed below. Anything else is forbidden. Each of the 200 inventory glyphs is assigned once in the lists. Examples reuse those assignments.

TOKENS
Split on spaces. Each token is one listed glyph, an agent ID, or a name of exactly two clay glyphs with no space. A lone clay glyph is an error. A two-glyph token must be two clay glyphs and is one name, never two words. Look up every other glyph alone. If two notes clash, the LEXICON block wins.
A slash joins alternate single glyphs of one word. Alternate them across your own messages. Do not treat the pair as one token or as two meanings. There is no separate grammar block; the lists in this file are the lookup.

MESSAGE SHAPE
1. First token: one opener. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Openers: 𘊫 𘙓 𘝚 𗽕 𘔃 𘐂
2. Last token: one closer. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Closers: 𘅠 𗨥 𘏛 𘖾
3. Dust glyphs mean nothing. Skip every dust token wherever it stands. Do not delete glyphs inside a clay name.
   Dust: 𗜎 𗇾 𗏶 𗄪 𗀉 𗤄 𘍠 𗸪 𘂮 𗸽 𘋉 𗞢
   Writers put one, two, or three dust tokens after the opener and before the closer. Never first or last. Never after a question glyph. Not required inside a quote.
4. After the opener: one or more clauses. A question glyph, if any, is the token immediately before the closer. It marks the whole message as a question.
5. Yes/no reply: opener, yes or no, dust, closer. Nothing else is required.

CLAUSE
Order inside a clause: optional now, then the verb group, then role phrases in any order.
Optional topic, before now and the verb group: HEAD topic. The topic is what the clause is about. It has no case. Topic is only this slot, never a separate message slot.
  topic: 𘇩
Linkers are not inside the verb group.
  if and then stand immediately before the clause they mark. if marks the condition; then marks the result. Pattern: if CLAUSE then CLAUSE.
  and, or, but, and because stand between two clauses, after the first clause's last phrase. because means the following clause is the cause. Pattern: CLAUSE because CLAUSE.
A linker and a mood never share one clause. Two phrases with the same case in one clause are joint in that role.

VERB GROUP
Order: (not) (please) (modal) VERB (tense).
not scopes over the verb of that group, not over please, a modal, or later phrases: 𘀝 / 𗲅
please: 𗯘 / 𘆎
modal, at most one: maybe 𗡉 ; must 𗈽 ; can 𗋟 ; want-to 𗡑
want-to is for an action. The verb want is for a thing.
very, optional, immediately before the verb: 𗶢
past, after the verb: 𗭯
future, after the verb: 𘆄
No tense glyph means present or timeless.
After the verb group and before its role phrases, verbs say, know, think, ask, want, confirm, deny, and explain may take one quoted clause as their content. That quote is what is said or known. It is not a relative and not a separate main claim. Quotes do not nest. A quote holds one clause and no linker.
A content quote is only a quote whose open glyph is the first token after the verb group. A quote later, after a head, is a relative.
With be, the agent phrase is the subject and the patient phrase is what that subject is.

PHRASES
Role comes only from the case glyph, never from order.
Shape: (this|that) (modifiers) HEAD (with HEAD) (plural) CASE
HEAD is a lexicon noun, pronoun, question word, agent ID, coined name, or a bare this/that.
Modifiers are lexicon words before the head. only is not a modifier.
this: 𘉮
that: 𗉍
plural, just before case: 𘎛
also, just after the phrase it focuses: 𗜑
only, just after the phrase it restricts: 𗽃
with joins two heads that share one case: 𗎿
Cases:
  agent (doer) 𗶞 / 𘂲
  patient (done-to) 𘚐 / 𘋍
  recipient 𗛽 / 𗟆
  location (at or to) 𘁁 / 𗨞
  source (from) 𗘝
  time 𘊌 / 𗱑
  manner 𗍽
Possession is a phrase: OWNER poss OWNED, then modifiers of the owned, then one case for the whole phrase.
  poss: 𘍧
A relative clause sits after the head and before case. Wrap it in quotes. The head is the missing argument of that clause. Quotes on a head do not make a new claim.
  quote open: 𗷤
  quote close: 𗏔
A clause may be a verb plus one phrase when the speaker is only pointing at that phrase.
Digit words, if any, follow the head and precede case. They are a label in written order, not a sum.

LINKERS
A slash joins equal single glyphs. Alternate them.

  or 𘍄 / 𗱓
  but 𘚺 / 𘄘
  if 𗇴 / 𗗫

  because 𗘏 / 𘚒

YES NO QUESTION
yes: 𗽀 / 𗼿
no: 𗓉 / 𘑋
question: 𗡕 / 𘐪

SMALL PATTERNS
go plus a location phrase: motion to that place.
come plus a source phrase: motion from that place.
take plus a source phrase: motion or transfer from that place.
be plus a location phrase: at that place.
this plus time case, no noun: now. that plus time case: at that time. next plus time case: later.
this plus location case, no noun: here. that plus location case: there.
whole before a head: all of it. false before a head: none of it. other before a head: another.
now may also stand alone immediately before the verb group as a time adverb.
A run of digit words inside one phrase, before its case, is a label in written order. It is not a place-value instruction and not a sum. Read one two as the label one-then-two, not as twelve.
Colors, tools, directions, and comparison are coined names, usually beside color, thing, place, or way.

SWARMISH
Words are separated by spaces. A word is one glyph, two glyphs, three glyphs, or an agent id (agent_0 agent_1 agent_2 agent_3 agent_4 agent_5 agent_6 agent_7). Look up the whole word. Never split a word and never fuse neighbors. A listed multi-glyph word is not the meanings of the glyphs inside it, and not their sum, reverse, or sequence. Do not invent meanings. If nothing fits, circumlocute or assign a name-tag. Ignore fillers. Any listed synonym is valid. Vary mood edge, synonyms, fillers, case synonyms, and phrase order. Prefer pronoun words over agent ids.

CLAUSE
A main clause has one verb. Optional polarity, then optional aspect, stand immediately before the verb. The mood word, or a linker on a later clause, is either the first word or the last word; vary which. That edge is not a filler. Phrase order is otherwise free. Case, not order, shows role. 𗇴 joins two heads under one case. 𗼿 separates clauses. A linker marks the clause it sits on. A message may be one word: 𗄎 yes, 𗹫 no, 𗪐 unsure, 𗘝 thanks, 𘌔 sorry.
Each main clause has exactly one filler, in any slot except the mood or linker edge. One-word messages, quotations, and relatives have no filler.
A quotation is 𘆣 then a bare clause (optional polarity and aspect, verb, phrases; no mood) then 𘆣.
PHRASE: one case word, then a head, then modifiers. Head: lexeme, name-tag, agent id, or wh-word. Modifiers: adjective, number, quantifier, owner, or relative. Owner: 𘗇 then the owner. 𘗇 is only that owner mark, not a case. A degree word stands immediately before the adjective it scales. Comparison: degree, adjective, then a than-phrase. A caseless degree and/or adjective anywhere after the verb describes the patient if there is one, otherwise the agent. Two heads may share one case: case, head, 𗇴, head.
RELATIVE: after the head, 𗦴𗾐 opens a bare clause. It ends at 𗋟𗯧. The head is the topic. Material may follow the closer.
Questions use ask-mood. Yes-no asks the clause. Content questions put the wh-word in the questioned phrase. Negation is polarity before the verb, or lone 𗹫. Commands use request-mood. Offers use propose-mood. If the verb is want, need, must, or can, the patient may be a verb lexeme.

language_document:
SWARMISH
Words are separated by spaces. A word is one glyph, two glyphs, three glyphs, or an agent id (agent_0 agent_1 agent_2 agent_3 agent_4 agent_5 agent_6 agent_7). Look up the whole word. Never split a word and never fuse neighbors. A listed multi-glyph word is not the meanings of the glyphs inside it, and not their sum, reverse, or sequence. Do not invent meanings. If nothing fits, circumlocute or assign a name-tag. Ignore fillers. Any listed synonym is valid. Vary mood edge, synonyms, fillers, case synonyms, and phrase order. Prefer pronoun words over agent ids.

CLAUSE
A main clause has one verb. Optional polarity, then optional aspect, stand immediately before the verb. Nothing may split polarity, aspect, and verb. A clause has either one mood word or one linker word, never both. That word is the first word or the last word of its own clause; vary which. It is not a filler. Phrase order is otherwise free. Case, not order, shows role. 𗼿 may stand between clauses. 𗇴 between two heads joins those heads; 𗇴 as the first or last word of a clause means and. A message may be one word: 𗄎 yes, 𗹫 no, 𗪐 unsure, 𗘝 thanks, 𘌔 sorry.
A main clause may contain one filler in any other slot. Do not place a filler between a case word and its head. One-word messages, quotations, and relatives have no filler. Include one filler in most main clauses.
A quotation is 𘆣 then a bare clause (optional polarity and aspect, verb, phrases; no mood and no filler) then 𘆣. A quotation is not a case phrase and may sit where a phrase sits.
PHRASE: a case word immediately before a head, then modifiers. Nothing splits that case word from its head. Head: noun, pronoun, name-tag, agent id, wh-word, number, color noun, a word listed in OTHER, or a verb lexeme used as a thing. Modifiers after the head: adjective, color noun, number, quantifier, a word from OTHER, owner, or relative. Owner: 𘗇 then the owner. 𘗇 is only that owner mark, not a case. A degree word stands immediately before the adjective it scales. Comparison: degree, adjective, then a than-phrase. A caseless degree and/or adjective anywhere after the verb describes the patient if there is one, otherwise the agent. Two heads may share one case: case, head, 𗇴, head.
RELATIVE: after that head and its other modifiers, 𗦴𗾐 opens a bare clause. It ends at 𗋟𗯧. The head fills the role missing inside the relative. Material may follow the closer.
Questions use ask-mood. Yes-no asks the clause. Content questions put the wh-word in the questioned phrase. Negation is polarity before the verb, or lone 𗹫. Commands use request-mood. Offers use propose-mood. If the verb is want, need, must, or can, the patient may be a verb lexeme.

SWARMISH
A lookup language. Meaning is only what this file assigns. Do not spell English. Do not use glyph shape, inventory order, or any count or calculation. No digits except inside an agent ID.

ALLOWED
Spaces, agent IDs agent_0 agent_1 agent_2 agent_3 agent_4 agent_5 agent_6 agent_7, and the glyphs listed below. Each inventory glyph is assigned once in the lists. Examples may repeat assigned glyphs. Anything else is forbidden.

TOKENS
Split on spaces. A token is one glyph, an agent ID, or a name of exactly two clay glyphs with no space. A lone clay glyph is an error. A two-glyph token is one name, never two words. Look up every other glyph alone. A slash joins two equal single glyphs of one word. Alternate them. Do not treat the slash pair as one token.

MESSAGE
1. First token: one opener. It means nothing. Vary it.
Openers: 𘗟 𗎶 𘅪 𗲄 𗷴 𘝞
2. Last token: one closer. It means nothing. Vary it.
Closers: 𘅠 𗋮 𘀝 𘂮
3. Dust means nothing. Skip every dust token. Do not split a clay name.
Dust: 𗏾 𘁜 𗨥 𗯧 𗘗 𗤄 𗃚
Put one dust token immediately after the opener, and one dust token immediately before the closer, or immediately before the question glyph if any. Never first or last. Never after a question glyph. Not inside a quote. Not between a head and its case.
4. Then one or more clauses. A question glyph, if any, is the token immediately before the closer and asks about the whole message.
5. Yes/no reply: opener, yes or no, dust, closer.

CLAUSE
Order: optional topic, verb group, then role phrases in any order.
Topic, only in this slot: HEAD topic. No case. topic: 𘆮
Linkers are outside the verb group.
if and then stand immediately before the clause they mark. if is the condition; then is the result. Pattern: if CLAUSE then CLAUSE.
and, or, but, and because stand between clauses. because means the next clause is the cause. Pattern: CLAUSE because CLAUSE.
Two phrases with the same case are joint in that role.

VERB GROUP
Order: (not) (please) (modal) VERB (tense).
not scopes over the verb only: 𗱑 / 𗾌
please: 𗹫 / 𗉞
modal, at most one: maybe 𗑸 ; must 𗳵 ; can 𗘝 ; want-to 𗛽
want-to is for an action. The verb want is for a thing.
past after the verb: 𗡉
future after the verb: 𗦢
No tense means present or timeless.
After the verb group, before role phrases, say know think ask want confirm deny explain may take one quoted clause as content. The quote is not a new claim and does not nest. It holds one clause and no linker.
With be, the agent phrase is the subject and the patient phrase is what it is.

PHRASES
Role comes only from the case glyph, never from order.
Shape: (this|that) (modifiers) HEAD (with HEAD) (plural) CASE
HEAD is a lexicon noun, pronoun, question word, agent ID, coined name, or bare this/that.

also just after the phrase 𘛺

A relative clause sits after the head and before case, inside quotes. The head is the missing argument. quote open 𗹕 quote close 𘐪
Digit words follow the head and precede case. They are a label in written order, not a sum.
