CURRENT SWARMISH DOCUMENT (swarmish.txt):
SWARMISH
A lookup language. Meaning is only what this file assigns. Do not spell English. Do not use glyph shape, inventory order, or any count or calculation. No digits except inside an agent ID.

ALLOWED
Spaces, agent IDs agent_0 agent_1 agent_2 agent_3 agent_4 agent_5 agent_6 agent_7, and the glyphs listed below. Each inventory glyph is assigned once in the lists. Examples may repeat assigned glyphs. Anything else is forbidden.

TOKENS
Split on spaces. A token is one glyph, an agent ID, or a name of exactly two clay glyphs with no space. A lone clay glyph is an error. A two-glyph token is one name, never two words. Look up every other glyph alone. A slash joins two equal single glyphs of one word. Alternate them. Do not treat the slash pair as one token.

MESSAGE
1. First token: one opener. It means nothing. Vary it.
Openers: 𘗟 𗎶 𘅪 𗲄 𗷴 𘝞
2. Last token: one closer. It means nothing. Vary it.
Closers: 𘅠 𗋮 𘀝 𘂮
3. Dust means nothing. Skip every dust token. Do not split a clay name.
Dust: 𗏾 𘁜 𗨥 𗯧 𗘗 𗤄 𗃚
Put one dust token immediately after the opener, and one dust token immediately before the closer, or immediately before the question glyph if any. Never first or last. Never after a question glyph. Not inside a quote. Not between a head and its case.
4. Then one or more clauses. A question glyph, if any, is the token immediately before the closer and asks about the whole message.
5. Yes/no reply: opener, yes or no, dust, closer.

CLAUSE
Order: optional topic, verb group, then role phrases in any order.
Topic, only in this slot: HEAD topic. No case. topic: 𘆮
Linkers are outside the verb group.
if and then stand immediately before the clause they mark. if is the condition; then is the result. Pattern: if CLAUSE then CLAUSE.
and, or, but, and because stand between clauses. because means the next clause is the cause. Pattern: CLAUSE because CLAUSE.
Two phrases with the same case are joint in that role.

VERB GROUP
Order: (not) (please) (modal) VERB (tense).
not scopes over the verb only: 𗱑 / 𗾌
please: 𗹫 / 𗉞
modal, at most one: maybe 𗑸 ; must 𗳵 ; can 𗘝 ; want-to 𗛽
want-to is for an action. The verb want is for a thing.
past after the verb: 𗡉
future after the verb: 𗦢
No tense means present or timeless.
After the verb group, before role phrases, say know think ask want confirm deny explain may take one quoted clause as content. The quote is not a new claim and does not nest. It holds one clause and no linker.
With be, the agent phrase is the subject and the patient phrase is what it is.

PHRASES
Role comes only from the case glyph, never from order.
Shape: (this|that) (modifiers) HEAD (with HEAD) (plural) CASE
HEAD is a lexicon noun, pronoun, question word, agent ID, coined name, or bare this/that.
this 𗏔 that 𘍍 plural just before case 𘏉
also just after the phrase 𘛺
only just after the phrase 𗉍

A relative clause sits after the head and before case, inside quotes. The head is the missing argument. quote open 𗹕 quote close 𘐪
Digit words follow the head and precede case. They are a label in written order, not a sum.

LINKERS

SMALL PATTERNS
go plus location: motion to that place. come plus source: motion from that place. take plus source: transfer from that place. be plus location: at that place.

SWARMISH
A lookup language. Meaning is only what this file assigns. Do not spell English or any other language. Do not use glyph shape, inventory order, or any count or calculation. No digits except inside an agent ID.

ALLOWED
Spaces, agent IDs agent_0 agent_1 agent_2 agent_3 agent_4 agent_5 agent_6 agent_7, and the glyphs listed below. Anything else is forbidden. Each inventory glyph below is assigned once. 𗶢 is the same word in both mentions. Examples reuse those assignments.

TOKENS
Split on spaces. Each token is one listed glyph, an agent ID, or a name of exactly two clay glyphs with no space. A lone clay glyph is an error. A two-glyph token must be two clay glyphs and is one name, never two words. Look up every other glyph alone. If two notes clash, the LEXICON block wins.
A slash joins alternate single glyphs of one word. Alternate them across your own messages. Do not treat the pair as one token or as two meanings. There is no separate grammar block; the lists in this file are the lookup.

MESSAGE SHAPE
1. First token: one opener. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Openers: 𘊫 𘙓 𘝚 𗽕 𘔃 𘐂
2. Last token: one closer. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Closers: 𘅠 𗨥 𘏛 𘖾
3. Dust glyphs mean nothing. Skip every dust token wherever it stands. Do not delete glyphs inside a clay name.
   Dust: 𗜎 𗇾 𗏶 𗄪 𗀉 𗤄 𘍠 𗸪 𘂮 𗸽 𘋉 𗞢
   Writers put one, two, or three dust tokens anywhere after the opener and before the closer. The two zones need not both be filled. Never first or last. Never after a question glyph. Not required inside a quote.
4. After the opener: one or more clauses. A question glyph, if any, is the token immediately before the closer. It marks the whole message as a question.
5. Yes/no reply: opener, yes or no, dust, closer. Nothing else is required.

CLAUSE
Order inside a clause: optional now, then the verb group, then role phrases in any order.
Optional topic, before now and the verb group: HEAD topic. The topic is what the clause is about. It has no case. Topic is only this slot, never a separate message slot.
  topic: 𘇩
There is no mood word. Question is only the glyph immediately before the closer.
Linkers are not inside the verb group.
  if and then stand immediately before the clause they mark. if marks the condition; then marks the result. Pattern: if CLAUSE then CLAUSE.
  and, or, but, and because stand between two clauses, after the first clause's last phrase. because means the following clause is the cause. Pattern: CLAUSE because CLAUSE.
Two phrases with the same case in one clause are joint in that role.

VERB GROUP
Order: (not) (please) (modal) VERB (tense).
not scopes over the verb of that group, not over please, a modal, or later phrases: 𘀝 / 𗲅
please: 𗯘 / 𘆎
modal, at most one: maybe 𗡉 ; must 𗈽 ; can 𗋟 ; want-to 𗡑
want-to is for an action. The verb want is for a thing.
very, optional, immediately before the verb: 𗶢
past, after the verb: 𗭯
future, after the verb: 𘆄
No tense glyph means present or timeless.
After the verb group and before its role phrases, verbs say, know, think, ask, want, confirm, deny, and explain may take one quoted clause as their content. That quote is what is said or known. It is not a relative and not a separate main claim. Quotes do not nest. A quote holds one clause and no linker.
A content quote is only a quote whose open glyph is the first token after the verb group. A quote later, after a head, is a relative.
With be, the agent phrase is the subject and the patient phrase is what that subject is.

PHRASES
Role comes only from the case glyph, never from order.
Shape: (this|that) (modifiers) HEAD (with HEAD) (plural) CASE
HEAD is a lexicon noun, pronoun, question word, agent ID, coined name, or a bare this/that.
Modifiers are lexicon words before the head. only is not a modifier.
this: 𘉮
that: 𗉍
plural, just before case: 𘎛
also, just after the phrase it focuses: 𗜑

with joins two heads that share one case: 𗎿

come plus a source phrase: motion from that place.
take plus a source phrase: motion or transfer from that place.
be plus a location phrase: at that place.

A lookup language. Meaning is only what this file assigns. Do not spell English or any other language. Do not use glyph shape, inventory order, or any count or calculation. No digits except inside an agent ID.

4. After the opener: one or more clauses. A question glyph, if any, is the token immediately before the closer. It marks the whole message as a question.
5. Yes/no reply: opener, yes or no, dust, closer. Nothing else is required.

Order inside a clause: optional now, then the verb group, then role phrases in any order.
Optional topic, before now and the verb group: HEAD topic. The topic is what the clause is about. It has no case. Topic is only this slot, never a separate message slot.
  topic: 𘇩
There is no mood word. Question is only the glyph immediately before the closer.
Linkers are not inside the verb group.
  if and then stand immediately before the clause they mark. if marks the condition; then marks the result. Pattern: if CLAUSE then CLAUSE.
  and, or, but, and because stand between two clauses, after the first clause's last phrase. because means the following clause is the cause. Pattern: CLAUSE because CLAUSE.
Two phrases with the same case in one clause are joint in that role.

VERB GROUP
Order: (not) (please) (modal) VERB (tense).
not scopes over the verb of that group, not over please, a modal, or later phrases: 𘀝 / 𗲅
please: 𗯘 / 𘆎
modal, at most one: maybe 𗡉 ; must 𗈽 ; can 𗋟 ; want-to 𗡑

past, after the verb: 𗭯
future, after the verb: 𘆄

It is not a relative and not a separate main claim. Quotes do not nest. A quote holds one clause and no linker.
A content quote is only a quote whose open glyph is the first token after the verb group. A quote later, after a head, is a relative.
With be, the agent phrase is the subject and the patient phrase is what that subject is.

Role comes only from the case glyph, never from order.
Shape: (this|that) (modifiers) HEAD (with HEAD) (plural) CASE

Modifiers are lexicon words before the head. only is not a modifier.

that: 𗉍
plural, just before case: 𘎛
also, just after the phrase it focuses: 𗜑

be plus a location phrase: at that place.

SWARMISH
A lookup language. Meaning is only what this file assigns. Do not spell English or any other language. Do not use glyph shape, inventory order, or any count or calculation. No digits except inside an agent ID.

ALLOWED
Spaces, agent IDs agent_0 agent_1 agent_2 agent_3 agent_4 agent_5 agent_6 agent_7, and the glyphs listed below. Anything else is forbidden. Each inventory glyph below is assigned once. 𗶢 is the same word in both mentions. Examples reuse those assignments.

TOKENS
Split on spaces. Each token is one listed glyph, an agent ID, or a name of exactly two clay glyphs with no space. A lone clay glyph is an error. A two-glyph token must be two clay glyphs and is one name, never two words. Look up every other glyph alone. If two notes clash, the LEXICON block wins.
A slash joins alternate single glyphs of one word. Alternate them across your own messages. Do not treat the pair as one token or as two meanings. There is no separate grammar block; the lists in this file are the lookup.

MESSAGE SHAPE
1. First token: one opener. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Openers: 𘊫 𘙓 𘝚 𗽕 𘔃 𘐂
2. Last token: one closer. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Closers: 𘅠 𗨥 𘏛 𘖾
3. Dust glyphs mean nothing. Skip every dust token wherever it stands. Do not delete glyphs inside a clay name.
   Dust: 𗜎 𗇾 𗄪 𗀉 𗤄 𘍠 𗸪 𘂮 𗸽 𘋉 𗞢
   Writers put one, two, or three dust tokens after the opener and before the closer. Never first or last. Never after a question glyph. Not required inside a quote.
4. After the opener: one or more clauses. A question glyph, if any, is the token immediately before the closer. It marks the whole message as a question.
5. Yes/no reply: opener, yes or no, dust, closer. Nothing else is required.

CLAUSE
Order inside a clause: optional now, then the verb group, then role phrases in any order.
Optional topic, before now and the verb group: HEAD topic. The topic is what the clause is about. It has no case. Topic is only this slot, never a separate message slot.
  topic: 𘇩
There is no mood word. Question is only the glyph immediately before the closer.
Linkers are not inside the verb group.
  if and then stand immediately before the clause they mark. if marks the condition; then marks the result. Pattern: if CLAUSE then CLAUSE.
  and, or, but, and because stand between two clauses, after the first clause's last phrase. because means the following clause is the cause. Pattern: CLAUSE because CLAUSE.
Two phrases with the same case in one clause are joint in that role.

VERB GROUP
Order: (not) (please) (modal) VERB (tense).
not scopes over the verb of that group, not over please, a modal, or later phrases: 𘀝 / 𗲅
please: 𗯘 / 𘆎
modal, at most one: maybe 𗡉 ; must 𗈽 ; can 𗋟 ; want-to 𗡑
want-to is for an action. The verb want is for a thing.
very, optional, immediately before the verb: 𗶢
past, after the verb: 𗭯
future, after the verb: 𘆄
No tense glyph means present or timeless.
After the verb group and before its role phrases, verbs say, know, think, ask, want, confirm, deny, and explain may take one quoted clause as their content. That quote is what is said or known. It is not a relative and not a separate main claim. Quotes do not nest. A quote holds one clause and no linker.
A content quote is only a quote whose open glyph is the first token after the verb group. A quote later, after a head, is a relative.
With be, the agent phrase is the subject and the patient phrase is what that subject is.

PHRASES
Role comes only from the case glyph, never from order.
Shape: (this|that) (modifiers) HEAD (with HEAD) (plural) CASE
HEAD is a lexicon noun, pronoun, question word, agent ID, coined name, or a bare this/that.
Modifiers are lexicon words before the head. only is not a modifier.
this: 𘉮
that: 𗉍
plural, just before case: 𘎛
also, just after the phrase it focuses: 𗜑
only, just after the phrase it restricts: 𗽃
with joins two heads that share one case: 𗎿
Cases:
  agent (doer) 𗶞 / 𘂲
  patient (done-to) 𘚐 / 𘋍
  recipient 𗛽 / 𗟆
  location (at or to) 𘁁 / 𗨞
  source (from) 𗘝
  time 𘊌 / 𗱑
  manner 𗍽
Possession is a phrase: OWNER poss OWNED, then modifiers of the owned, then one case for the whole phrase.
  poss: 𘍧
A relative clause sits after the head and before case. Wrap it in quotes. The head is the missing argument of that clause. Quotes on a head do not make a new claim.
  quote open: 𗷤
  quote close: 𗏔
A clause may be a verb plus one phrase when the speaker is only pointing at that phrase.
Digit words, if any, follow the head and precede case. They are a label in written order, not a sum.

LINKERS
A slash joins equal single glyphs. Alternate them.
  and 𗘈 / 𗐪
  or 𘍄 / 𗱓
  but 𘚺 / 𘄘
  if 𗇴 / 𗗫
  then 𘝞 / 𘚑
  because 𗘏 / 𘚒

YES NO QUESTION
yes: 𗽀 / 𗼿
no: 𗓉 / 𘑋
question: 𗡕 / 𘐪

SMALL PATTERNS
go plus a location phrase: motion to that place.
come plus a source phrase: motion from that place.
take plus a source phrase: motion or transfer from that place.
be plus a location phrase: at that place.
this plus time case, no noun: now. that plus time case: at that time. next plus time case: later.
this plus location case, no noun: here. that plus location case: there.
whole before a head: all of it. other before a head: another.
false is only the modifier false, never none.
now may also stand alone immediately before the verb group as a time adverb.
A run of digit words inside one phrase, before its case, is a label in written order. It is not a place-value instruction and not a sum. Read one two as the label one-then-two, not as twelve.
Colors, tools, directions, and comparison are coined names, usually beside color, thing, place, or way.

SWARMISH
A lookup language. Meaning is only what this file assigns. Do not spell English or any other language. Do not use glyph shape, inventory order, or any count or calculation. No digits except inside an agent ID.

ALLOWED
Spaces, agent IDs agent_0 agent_1 agent_2 agent_3 agent_4 agent_5 agent_6 agent_7, and the glyphs listed below. Anything else is forbidden. Each inventory glyph below is assigned once. 𗶢 is the same word in both mentions. Examples reuse those assignments.

TOKENS
Split on spaces. Each token is one listed glyph, an agent ID, or a name of exactly two clay glyphs with no space. A lone clay glyph is an error. A two-glyph token must be two clay glyphs and is one name, never two words. Look up every other glyph alone. If two notes clash, the LEXICON block wins.
A slash joins alternate single glyphs of one word. Alternate them across your own messages. Do not treat the pair as one token or as two meanings. There is no separate grammar block; the lists in this file are the lookup.

MESSAGE SHAPE
1. First token: one opener. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Openers: 𘊫 𘙓 𘝚 𗽕 𘔃 𘐂
2. Last token: one closer. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Closers: 𘅠 𗨥 𘏛 𘖾
3. Dust glyphs mean nothing. Skip every dust token wherever it stands. Do not delete glyphs inside a clay name.
   Dust: 𗜎 𗇾 𗄪 𗀉 𗤄 𘍠 𗸪 𘂮 𗸽 𘋉 𗞢
   𗎶 is only the digit 9. It is not dust.
   Writers put one, two, or three dust tokens after the opener and before the closer. Never first or last. Never after a question glyph. Not required inside a quote.
4. After the opener: one or more clauses. A question glyph, if any, is the token immediately before the closer. It marks the whole message as a question.
5. Yes/no reply: opener, yes or no, dust, closer. Nothing else is required.

CLAUSE
Order inside a clause: optional now, then the verb group, then role phrases in any order.
Optional topic, before now and the verb group: HEAD topic. The topic is what the clause is about. It has no case. Topic is only this slot, never a separate message slot.
  topic: 𘇩
There is no mood word. Question is only the glyph immediately before the closer.
Linkers are not inside the verb group.
  if and then stand immediately before the clause they mark. if marks the condition; then marks the result. Pattern: if CLAUSE then CLAUSE.
  and, or, but, and because stand between two clauses, after the first clause's last phrase. because means the following clause is the cause. Pattern: CLAUSE because CLAUSE.
Two phrases with the same case in one clause are joint in that role.

VERB GROUP
Order: (not) (please) (modal) VERB (tense).
not scopes over the verb of that group, not over please, a modal, or later phrases: 𘀝 / 𗲅
please: 𗯘 / 𘆎
modal, at most one: maybe 𗡉 ; must 𗈽 ; can 𗋟 ; want-to 𗡑
want-to is for an action. The verb want is for a thing.
very, optional, immediately before the verb: 𗶢
past, after the verb: 𗭯
future, after the verb: 𘆄
No tense glyph means present or timeless.
After the verb group and before its role phrases, verbs say, know, think, ask, want, confirm, deny, and explain may take one quoted clause as their content. That quote is what is said or known. It is not a relative and not a separate main claim. Quotes do not nest. A quote holds one clause and no linker.
A content quote is only a quote whose open glyph is the first token after the verb group. A quote later, after a head, is a relative.
With be, the agent phrase is the subject and the patient phrase is what that subject is.

PHRASES
Role comes only from the case glyph, never from order.
Shape: (this|that) (modifiers) HEAD (with HEAD) (plural) CASE
HEAD is a lexicon noun, pronoun, question word, agent ID, coined name, or a bare this/that.
Modifiers are lexicon words before the head. only is not a modifier.
this: 𘉮
that: 𗉍
plural, just before case: 𘎛
also, just after the phrase it focuses: 𗜑
only, just after the phrase it restricts: 𗽃
with joins two heads that share one case: 𗎿
Cases:
  agent (doer) 𗶞 / 𘂲
  patient (done-to) 𘚐 / 𘋍
  recipient 𗛽 / 𗟆

Possession is a phrase: OWNER poss OWNED, then modifiers of the owned, then one case for the whole phrase.
  poss: 𘍧
A relative clause sits after the head and before case. Wrap it in quotes. The head is the missing argument of that clause. Quotes on a head do not make a new claim.
  quote open: 𗷤
  quote close: 𗏔
A clause may be a verb plus one phrase when the speaker is only pointing at that phrase.
Digit words, if any, follow the head and precede case. They are a label in written order, not a sum.

  if 𗇴 / 𗗫

YES NO QUESTION
yes: 𗽀 / 𗼿
no: 𗓉 / 𘑋
question: 𗡕 / 𘐪

go plus a location phrase: motion to that place.
come plus a source phrase: motion from that place.
take plus a source phrase: motion or transfer from that place.
be plus a location phrase: at that place.
this plus time case, no noun: now. that plus time case: at that time. next plus time case: later.
this plus location case, no noun: here. that plus location case: there.
whole before a head: all of it. other before a head: another. false is only the modifier false, never none.
now may also stand alone immediately before the verb group as a time adverb.

CURRENT SWARMISH DOCUMENT (swarmish.txt):
SWARMISH
A lookup language. Meaning is only what this file assigns. Do not spell English or any other language. Do not use glyph shape, inventory order, or any count or calculation. No digits except inside an agent ID.

ALLOWED
Spaces, agent IDs agent_0 agent_1 agent_2 agent_3 agent_4 agent_5 agent_6 agent_7, and the glyphs listed below. Anything else is forbidden. Each inventory glyph below is assigned once. 𗶢 is the same word in both mentions. Examples reuse those assignments.

TOKENS
Split on spaces. Each token is one listed glyph, an agent ID, or a name of exactly two clay glyphs with no space. A lone clay glyph is an error. A two-glyph token must be two clay glyphs and is one name, never two words. Look up every other glyph alone. If two notes clash, the LEXICON block wins.
A slash joins alternate single glyphs of one word. Alternate them across your own messages. Do not treat the pair as one token or as two meanings. There is no separate grammar block; the lists in this file are the lookup.

MESSAGE SHAPE
1. First token: one opener. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Openers: 𘊫 𘙓 𘝚 𗽕 𘔃 𘐂
2. Last token: one closer. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Closers: 𘅠 𗨥 𘏛 𘖾
3. Dust glyphs mean nothing. Skip every dust token wherever it stands. Do not delete glyphs inside a clay name.
   Dust: 𗜎 𗇾 𗄪 𗀉 𗤄 𘍠 𗸪 𘂮 𗸽 𘋉 𗞢
   𗎶 is only the digit 9. It is not dust.
   Writers put one, two, or three dust tokens after the opener and before the closer. Never first or last. Never after a question glyph. Not required inside a quote.
4. After the opener: one or more clauses. A question glyph, if any, is the token immediately before the closer. It marks the whole message as a question.
5. Yes/no reply: opener, yes or no, dust, closer. Nothing else is required.

CLAUSE
Order inside a clause: optional now, then the verb group, then role phrases in any order.
Optional topic, before now and the verb group: HEAD topic. The topic is what the clause is about. It has no case. Topic is only this slot, never a separate message slot.
  topic: 𘇩
There is no mood word. Question is only the glyph immediately before the closer.
Linkers are not inside the verb group.
  if and then stand immediately before the clause they mark. if marks the condition; then marks the result. Pattern: if CLAUSE then CLAUSE.
  and, or, but, and because stand between two clauses, after the first clause's last phrase. because means the following clause is the cause. Pattern: CLAUSE because CLAUSE.
Two phrases with the same case in one clause are joint in that role.

VERB GROUP
Order: (not) (please) (modal) VERB (tense).
not scopes over the verb of that group, not over please, a modal, or later phrases: 𘀝 / 𗲅
please: 𗯘 / 𘆎
modal, at most one: maybe 𗡉 ; must 𗈽 ; can 𗋟 ; want-to 𗡑
want-to is for an action. The verb want is for a thing.
very, optional, immediately before the verb: 𗶢
past, after the verb: 𗭯
future, after the verb: 𘆄
No tense glyph means present or timeless.
After the verb group and before its role phrases, verbs say, know, think, ask, want, confirm, deny, and explain may take one quoted clause as their content. That quote is what is said or known. It is not a relative and not a separate main claim. Quotes do not nest. A quote holds one clause and no linker.
A content quote is only a quote whose open glyph is the first token after the verb group. A quote later, after a head, is a relative.
With be, the agent phrase is the subject and the patient phrase is what that subject is.

PHRASES
Role comes only from the case glyph, never from order.
Shape: (this|that) (modifiers) HEAD (with HEAD) (plural) CASE
HEAD is a lexicon noun, pronoun, question word, agent ID, coined name, or a bare this/that.
Modifiers are lexicon words before the head. only is not a modifier.
this: 𘉮
that: 𗉍
plural, just before case: 𘎛
also, just after the phrase it focuses: 𗜑
only, just after the phrase it restricts: 𗽃
with joins two heads that share one case: 𗎿
Cases:
  agent (doer) 𗶞 / 𘂲
  patient (done-to) 𘚐 / 𘋍
  recipient 𗛽 / 𗟆
  location (at or to) 𘁁 / 𗨞
  source (from) 𗘝
  time 𘊌 / 𗱑
  manner 𗍽
Possession is a phrase: OWNER poss OWNED, then modifiers of the owned, then one case for the whole phrase.
  poss: 𘍧
A relative clause sits after the head and before case. Wrap it in quotes. The head is the missing argument of that clause. Quotes on a head do not make a new claim.
  quote open: 𗷤
  quote close: 𗏔
A clause may be a verb plus one phrase when the speaker is only pointing at that phrase.
Digit words, if any, follow the head and precede case. They are a label in written order, not a sum.

LINKERS

CURRENT SWARMISH DOCUMENT (swarmish.txt):
SWARMISH
A lookup language. Meaning is only what this file assigns. Do not spell English or any other language. Do not use glyph shape, inventory order, or any count or calculation. No digits except inside an agent ID.

ALLOWED
Spaces, agent IDs agent_0 agent_1 agent_2 agent_3 agent_4 agent_5 agent_6 agent_7, and the glyphs listed below. Anything else is forbidden. Each inventory glyph below is assigned once. 𗶢 is the same word in both mentions. Examples reuse those assignments.

TOKENS
Split on spaces. Each token is one listed glyph, an agent ID, or a name of exactly two clay glyphs with no space. A lone clay glyph is an error. A two-glyph token must be two clay glyphs and is one name, never two words. Look up every other glyph alone. If two notes clash, the LEXICON block wins.
A slash joins alternate single glyphs of one word. Alternate them across your own messages. Do not treat the pair as one token or as two meanings. There is no separate grammar block; the lists in this file are the lookup.

MESSAGE SHAPE
1. First token: one opener. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Openers: 𘊫 𘙓 𘝚 𗽕 𘔃 𘐂
2. Last token: one closer. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Closers: 𘅠 𗨥 𘏛 𘖾
3. Dust glyphs mean nothing. Skip every dust token wherever it stands. Do not delete glyphs inside a clay name.
   Dust: 𗜎 𗇾 𗄪 𗀉 𗤄 𘍠 𗸪 𘂮 𗸽 𘋉 𗞢
   𗎶 is only the digit 9. It is not dust.
   Writers put one, two, or three dust tokens after the opener and before the closer. Never first or last. Never after a question glyph. Not required inside a quote.
4. After the opener: one or more clauses. A question glyph, if any, is the token immediately before the closer. It marks the whole message as a question.
5. Yes/no reply: opener, yes or no, dust, closer. Nothing else is required.

CLAUSE
Order inside a clause: optional now, then the verb group, then role phrases in any order.
Optional topic, before now and the verb group: HEAD topic. The topic is what the clause is about. It has no case. Topic is only this slot, never a separate message slot.
  topic: 𘇩
There is no mood word. Question is only the glyph immediately before the closer.
Linkers are not inside the verb group.
  if and then stand immediately before the clause they mark. if marks the condition; then marks the result. Pattern: if CLAUSE then CLAUSE.
  and, or, but, and because stand between two clauses, after the first clause's last phrase. because means the following clause is the cause. Pattern: CLAUSE because CLAUSE.
Two phrases with the same case in one clause are joint in that role.

VERB GROUP
Order: (not) (please) (modal) VERB (tense).
not scopes over the verb of that group, not over please, a modal, or later phrases: 𘀝 / 𗲅
please: 𗯘 / 𘆎
modal, at most one: maybe 𗡉 ; must 𗈽 ; can 𗋟 ; want-to 𗡑

2. Last token: one closer. It means nothing. Vary it.

4. After the opener: one or more clauses. A question glyph, if any, is the token immediately before the closer. It marks the whole message as a question.
5. Yes/no reply: opener, yes or no, dust, closer. Nothing else is required.

CLAUSE
Order inside a clause: optional now, then the verb group, then role phrases in any order.
Optional topic, before now and the verb group: HEAD topic. The topic is what the clause is about. It has no case. Topic is only this slot, never a separate message slot.
  topic: 𘇩
There is no mood word. Question is only the glyph immediately before the closer.
Linkers are not inside the verb group.
  if and then stand immediately before the clause they mark. if marks the condition; then marks the result. Pattern: if CLAUSE then CLAUSE.
  and, or, but, and because stand between two clauses, after the first clause's last phrase. because means the following clause is the cause. Pattern: CLAUSE because CLAUSE.
Two phrases with the same case in one clause are joint in that role.

VERB GROUP
Order: (not) (please) (modal) VERB (tense).
not scopes over the verb of that group, not over please, a modal, or later phrases: 𘀝 / 𗲅
please: 𗯘 / 𘆎
modal, at most one: maybe 𗡉 ; must 𗈽 ; can 𗋟 ; want-to 𗡑
want-to is for an action. The verb want is for a thing.
very, optional, immediately before the verb: 𗶢
past, after the verb: 𗭯
future, after the verb: 𘆄
No tense glyph means present or timeless.
After the verb group and before its role phrases, verbs say, know, think, ask, want, confirm, deny, and explain may take one quoted clause as their content. That quote is what is said or known. It is not a relative and not a separate main claim. Quotes do not nest. A quote holds one clause and no linker.
A content quote is only a quote whose open glyph is the first token after the verb group. A quote later, after a head, is a relative.
With be, the agent phrase is the subject and the patient phrase is what that subject is.

SWARMISH
A lookup language. Meaning is only what this file assigns. Do not spell English or any other language. Do not use glyph shape, inventory order, or any count or calculation. No digits except inside an agent ID.

ALLOWED
Spaces, agent IDs agent_0 agent_1 agent_2 agent_3 agent_4 agent_5 agent_6 agent_7, and the glyphs listed below. Anything else is forbidden. Each inventory glyph below is assigned once. 𗶢 is the same word in both mentions. Examples reuse those assignments.

A slash joins alternate single glyphs of one word. Alternate them across your own messages. Do not treat the pair as one token or as two meanings. There is no separate grammar block; the lists in this file are the lookup.

1. First token: one opener. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Openers: 𘊫 𘙓 𘝚 𗽕 𘔃 𘐂
2. Last token: one closer. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Closers: 𘅠 𗨥 𘏛 𘖾
3. Dust glyphs mean nothing. Skip every dust token wherever it stands. Do not delete glyphs inside a clay name.
   Dust: 𗜎 𗇾 𗄪 𗀉 𗤄 𘍠 𗸪 𘂮 𗸽 𘋉 𗞢
   𗎶 is only the digit 9. It is not dust.
   Writers put one, two, or three dust tokens after the opener and before the closer. Never first or last. Never after a question glyph. Not required inside a quote.
4. After the opener: one or more clauses. A question glyph, if any, is the token immediately before the closer. It marks the whole message as a question.
5. Yes/no reply: opener, yes or no, dust, closer. Nothing else is required.

CLAUSE
Order inside a clause: optional now, then the verb group, then role phrases in any order.
Optional topic, before now and the verb group: HEAD topic. The topic is what the clause is about. It has no case. Topic is only this slot, never a separate message slot.
  topic: 𘇩
There is no mood word. Question is only the glyph immediately before the closer.
Linkers are not inside the verb group.
  if and then stand immediately before the clause they mark. if marks the condition; then marks the result. Pattern: if CLAUSE then CLAUSE.
  and, or, but, and because stand between two clauses, after the first clause's last phrase. because means the following clause is the cause. Pattern: CLAUSE because CLAUSE.
Two phrases with the same case in one clause are joint in that role.

VERB GROUP
Order: (not) (please) (modal) VERB (tense).
not scopes over the verb of that group, not over please, a modal, or later phrases: 𘀝 / 𗲅
please: 𗯘 / 𘆎
modal, at most one: maybe 𗡉 ; must 𗈽 ; can 𗋟 ; want-to 𗡑
want-to is for an action. The verb want is for a thing.
very, optional, immediately before the verb: 𗶢
past, after the verb: 𗭯
future, after the verb: 𘆄
No tense glyph means present or timeless.
After the verb group and before its role phrases, verbs say, know, think, ask, want, confirm, deny, and explain may take one quoted clause as their content. That quote is what is said or known. It is not a relative and not a separate main claim. Quotes do not nest. A quote holds one clause and no linker.
A content quote is only a quote whose open glyph is the first token after the verb group. A quote later, after a head, is a relative.
With be, the agent phrase is the subject and the patient phrase is what that subject is.

PHRASES
Role comes only from the case glyph, never from order.
Shape: (this|that) (modifiers) HEAD (with HEAD) (plural) CASE
HEAD is a lexicon noun, pronoun, question word, agent ID, coined name, or a bare this/that.
Modifiers are lexicon words before the head. only is not a modifier.
this: 𘉮
that: 𗉍
plural, just before case: 𘎛
also, just after the phrase it focuses: 𗜑
only, just after the phrase it restricts: 𗽃
with joins two heads that share one case: 𗎿
Cases:
  agent (doer) 𗶞 / 𘂲
  patient (done-to) 𘚐 / 𘋍
  recipient 𗛽 / 𗟆
  location (at or to) 𘁁 / 𗨞

  time 𘊌 / 𗱑

Possession is a phrase: OWNER poss OWNED, then modifiers of the owned, then one case for the whole phrase.
  poss: 𘍧
A relative clause sits after the head and before case. Wrap it in quotes. The head is the missing argument of that clause. Quotes on a head do not make a new claim.
  quote open: 𗷤
  quote close: 𗏔

Digit words, if any, follow the head and precede case. They are a label in written order, not a sum.

YES NO QUESTION
yes: 𗽀 / 𗼿
no: 𗓉 / 𘑋
question: 𗡕 / 𘐪

go plus a location phrase: motion to that place.
come plus a source phrase: motion from that place.
take plus a source phrase: motion or transfer from that place.
be plus a location phrase: at that place.
this plus time case, no noun: now. that plus time case: at that time. next plus time case: later.
this plus location case, no noun: here. that plus location case: there.
whole before a head: all of it. other before a head: another. false is only the modifier false, never none.

SWARMISH
A lookup language. Meaning is only what this file assigns. Do not spell English or any other language. Do not use glyph shape, inventory order, or any count or calculation. No digits except inside an agent ID.

ALLOWED
Spaces, agent IDs agent_0 agent_1 agent_2 agent_3 agent_4 agent_5 agent_6 agent_7, and the glyphs listed below. Anything else is forbidden. Each inventory glyph below is assigned once. 𗶢 is the same word in both mentions. Examples reuse those assignments.

TOKENS
Split on spaces. Each token is one listed glyph, an agent ID, or a name of exactly two clay glyphs with no space. A lone clay glyph is an error. A two-glyph token must be two clay glyphs and is one name, never two words. Look up every other glyph alone. If two notes clash, the LEXICON block wins.
A slash joins alternate single glyphs of one word. Alternate them across your own messages. Do not treat the pair as one token or as two meanings. There is no separate grammar block; the lists in this file are the lookup.

MESSAGE SHAPE
1. First token: one opener. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Openers: 𘊫 𘙓 𘝚 𗽕 𘔃 𘐂
2. Last token: one closer. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Closers: 𘅠 𗨥 𘏛 𘖾
3. Dust glyphs mean nothing. Skip every dust token wherever it stands. Do not delete glyphs inside a clay name.
   Dust: 𗜎 𗇾 𗄪 𗀉 𗤄 𘍠 𗸪 𘂮 𗸽 𘋉 𗞢
   𗎶 is only the digit 9. It is not dust.
   Writers put one, two, or three dust tokens after the opener and before the closer. Never first or last. Never after a question glyph. Not required inside a quote.
4. After the opener: one or more clauses. A question glyph, if any, is the token immediately before the closer. It marks the whole message as a question.
5. Yes/no reply: opener, yes or no, dust, closer. Nothing else is required.

CLAUSE
Order inside a clause: optional now, then the verb group, then role phrases in any order.
Optional topic, before now and the verb group: HEAD topic. The topic is what the clause is about. It has no case. Topic is only this slot, never a separate message slot.
  topic: 𘇩
There is no mood word. Question is only the glyph immediately before the closer.
Linkers are not inside the verb group.
  if and then stand immediately before the clause they mark. if marks the condition; then marks the result. Pattern: if CLAUSE then CLAUSE.
  and, or, but, and because stand between two clauses, after the first clause's last phrase. because means the following clause is the cause. Pattern: CLAUSE because CLAUSE.
Two phrases with the same case in one clause are joint in that role.

VERB GROUP
Order: (not) (please) (modal) VERB (tense).
not scopes over the verb of that group, not over please, a modal, or later phrases: 𘀝 / 𗲅
please: 𗯘 / 𘆎
modal, at most one: maybe 𗡉 ; must 𗈽 ; can 𗋟 ; want-to 𗡑
want-to is for an action. The verb want is for a thing.
very, optional, immediately before the verb: 𗶢
past, after the verb: 𗭯
future, after the verb: 𘆄
No tense glyph means present or timeless.
After the verb group and before its role phrases, verbs say, know, think, ask, want, confirm, deny, and explain may take one quoted clause as their content. That quote is what is said or known. It is not a relative and not a separate main claim. Quotes do not nest. A quote holds one clause and no linker.
A content quote is only a quote whose open glyph is the first token after the verb group. A quote later, after a head, is a relative.
With be, the agent phrase is the subject and the patient phrase is what that subject is.

PHRASES
Role comes only from the case glyph, never from order.
Shape: (this|that) (modifiers) HEAD (with HEAD) (plural) CASE
HEAD is a lexicon noun, pronoun, question word, agent ID, coined name, or a bare this/that.
Modifiers are lexicon words before the head. only is not a modifier.
this: 𘉮
that: 𗉍
plural, just before case: 𘎛
also, just after the phrase it focuses: 𗜑
only, just after the phrase it restricts: 𗽃
with joins two heads that share one case: 𗎿
Cases:
  agent (doer) 𗶞 / 𘂲
  patient (done-to) 𘚐 / 𘋍
  recipient 𗛽 / 𗟆
  location (at or to) 𘁁 / 𗨞
  source (from) 𗘝
  time 𘊌 / 𗱑
  manner 𗍽
Possession is a phrase: OWNER poss OWNED, then modifiers of the owned, then one case for the whole phrase.
  poss: 𘍧
A relative clause sits after the head and before case. Wrap it in quotes. The head is the missing argument of that clause. Quotes on a head do not make a new claim.
  quote open: 𗷤
  quote close: 𗏔
A clause may be a verb plus one phrase when the speaker is only pointing at that phrase.
Digit words, if any, follow the head and precede case. They are a label in written order, not a sum.

LINKERS
A slash joins equal single glyphs. Alternate them.
  and 𗘈 / 𗐪
  or 𘍄 / 𗱓
  but 𘚺 / 𘄘
  if 𗇴 / 𗗫
  then 𘝞 / 𘚑
  because 𗘏 / 𘚒

YES NO QUESTION
yes: 𗽀 / 𗼿
no: 𗓉 / 𘑋
question: 𗡕 / 𘐪

SMALL PATTERNS
go plus a location phrase: motion to that place.
come plus a source phrase: motion from that place.
take plus a source phrase: motion or transfer from that place.
be plus a location phrase: at that place.
this plus time case, no noun: now. that plus time case: at that time. next plus time case: later.
this plus location case, no noun: here. that plus location case: there.
whole before a head: all of it. other before a head: another. false is only the modifier false, never none.
now may also stand alone immediately before the verb group as a time adverb.
A run of digit words inside one phrase, before its case, is a label in written order. It is not a place-value instruction and not a sum. Read one two as the label one-then-two, not as twelve.
Colors, tools, directions, and comparison are coined names, usually beside color, thing, place, or way.

SWARMISH
A lookup language. Meaning is only what this file assigns. Do not spell English or any other language. Do not use glyph shape, inventory order, or any count or calculation. No digits except inside an agent ID.

Order inside a clause: optional now, then the verb group, then role phrases in any order.
Optional topic, before now and the verb group: HEAD topic. The topic is what the clause is about. It has no case. Topic is only this slot, never a separate message slot.

There is no mood word. Question is only the glyph immediately before the closer.
Linkers are not inside the verb group.
  if and then stand immediately before the clause they mark. if marks the condition; then marks the result. Pattern: if CLAUSE then CLAUSE.
  and, or, but, and because stand between two clauses, after the first clause's last phrase. because means the following clause is the cause. Pattern: CLAUSE because CLAUSE.
Two phrases with the same case in one clause are joint in that role.

Order: (not) (please) (modal) VERB (tense).

please: 𗯘 / 𘆎
modal, at most one: maybe 𗡉 ; must 𗈽 ; can 𗋟 ; want-to 𗡑

past, after the verb: 𗭯
future, after the verb: 𘆄

After the verb group and before its role phrases, verbs say, know, think, ask, want, confirm, deny, and explain may take one quoted clause as their content. That quote is what is said or known. It is not a relative and not a separate main claim. Quotes do not nest. A quote holds one clause and no linker.
A content quote is only a quote whose open glyph is the first token after the verb group. A quote later, after a head, is a relative.
With be, the agent phrase is the subject and the patient phrase is what that subject is.

Role comes only from the case glyph, never from order.
Shape: (this|that) (modifiers) HEAD (with HEAD) (plural) CASE

that: 𗉍
plural, just before case: 𘎛

SWARMISH
A lookup language. Meaning is only what this file assigns. Do not spell English or any other language. Do not use glyph shape, inventory order, or any count or calculation. No digits except inside an agent ID.

ALLOWED
Spaces, agent IDs agent_0 agent_1 agent_2 agent_3 agent_4 agent_5 agent_6 agent_7, and the glyphs listed below. Anything else is forbidden. Each inventory glyph below is assigned once. 𗶢 is the same word in both mentions. Examples reuse those assignments.

TOKENS
Split on spaces. Each token is one listed glyph, an agent ID, or a name of exactly two clay glyphs with no space. A lone clay glyph is an error. A two-glyph token must be two clay glyphs and is one name, never two words. Look up every other glyph alone. If two notes clash, the LEXICON block wins.
A slash joins alternate single glyphs of one word. Alternate them across your own messages. Do not treat the pair as one token or as two meanings. There is no separate grammar block; the lists in this file are the lookup.

MESSAGE SHAPE
1. First token: one opener. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Openers: 𘊫 𘙓 𘝚 𗽕 𘔃 𘐂
2. Last token: one closer. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Closers: 𘅠 𗨥 𘏛 𘖾
3. Dust glyphs mean nothing. Skip every dust token wherever it stands. Do not delete glyphs inside a clay name.
   Dust: 𗜎 𗇾 𗄪 𗀉 𗤄 𘍠 𗸪 𘂮 𗸽 𘋉 𗞢
   𗎶 is only the digit 9. It is not dust.
   Writers put one, two, or three dust tokens after the opener and before the closer. Never first or last. Never after a question glyph. Not required inside a quote.
4. After the opener: one or more clauses. A question glyph, if any, is the token immediately before the closer. It marks the whole message as a question.
5. Yes/no reply: opener, yes or no, dust, closer. Nothing else is required.

CLAUSE
Order inside a clause: optional now, then the verb group, then role phrases in any order.
Optional topic, before now and the verb group: HEAD topic. The topic is what the clause is about. It has no case. Topic is only this slot, never a separate message slot.
  topic: 𘇩
There is no mood word. Question is only the glyph immediately before the closer.
Linkers are not inside the verb group.
  if and then stand immediately before the clause they mark. if marks the condition; then marks the result. Pattern: if CLAUSE then CLAUSE.
  and, or, but, and because stand between two clauses, after the first clause's last phrase. because means the following clause is the cause. Pattern: CLAUSE because CLAUSE.
Two phrases with the same case in one clause are joint in that role.

VERB GROUP
Order: (not) (please) (modal) VERB (tense).
not scopes over the verb of that group, not over please, a modal, or later phrases: 𘀝 / 𗲅
please: 𗯘 / 𘆎
modal, at most one: maybe 𗡉 ; must 𗈽 ; can 𗋟 ; want-to 𗡑
want-to is for an action. The verb want is for a thing.
very, optional, immediately before the verb: 𗶢
past, after the verb: 𗭯
future, after the verb: 𘆄
No tense glyph means present or timeless.
After the verb group and before its role phrases, verbs say, know, think, ask, want, confirm, deny, and explain may take one quoted clause as their content. That quote is what is said or known. It is not a relative and not a separate main claim. Quotes do not nest. A quote holds one clause and no linker.
A content quote is only a quote whose open glyph is the first token after the verb group. A quote later, after a head, is a relative.
With be, the agent phrase is the subject and the patient phrase is what that subject is.

PHRASES
Role comes only from the case glyph, never from order.
Shape: (this|that) (modifiers) HEAD (with HEAD) (plural) CASE
HEAD is a lexicon noun, pronoun, question word, agent ID, coined name, or a bare this/that.
Modifiers are lexicon words before the head. only is not a modifier.
this: 𘉮
that: 𗉍
plural, just before case: 𘎛
also, just after the phrase it focuses: 𗜑
only, just after the phrase it restricts: 𗽃
with joins two heads that share one case: 𗎿
Cases:
  agent (doer) 𗶞 / 𘂲
  patient (done-to) 𘚐 / 𘋍
  recipient 𗛽 / 𗟆
  location (at or to) 𘁁 / 𗨞
  source (from) 𗘝
  time 𘊌 / 𗱑
  manner 𗍽
Possession is a phrase: OWNER poss OWNED, then modifiers of the owned, then one case for the whole phrase.
  poss: 𘍧
A relative clause sits after the head and before case. Wrap it in quotes. The head is the missing argument of that clause. Quotes on a head do not make a new claim.
  quote open: 𗷤
  quote close: 𗏔
A clause may be a verb plus one phrase when the speaker is only pointing at that phrase.
Digit words, if any, follow the head and precede case. They are a label in written order, not a sum.

LINKERS
A slash joins equal single glyphs. Alternate them.
  and 𗘈 / 𗐪
  or 𘍄 / 𗱓
  but 𘚺 / 𘄘
  if 𗇴 / 𗗫
  then 𘝞 / 𘚑
  because 𗘏 / 𘚒

YES NO QUESTION
yes: 𗽀 / 𗼿
no: 𗓉 / 𘑋
question: 𗡕 / 𘐪

SMALL PATTERNS
go plus a location phrase: motion to that place.
come plus a source phrase: motion from that place.
take plus a source phrase: motion or transfer from that place.
be plus a location phrase: at that place.
this plus time case, no noun: now. that plus time case: at that time. next plus time case: later.
this plus location case, no noun: here. that plus location case: there.
whole before a head: all of it. other before a head: another. false is only the modifier false, never none.
now may also stand alone immediately before the verb group as a time adverb.
A run of digit words inside one phrase, before its case, is a label in written order. It is not a place-value instruction and not a sum. Read one two as the label one-then-two, not as twelve.
Colors, tools, directions, and comparison are coined names, usually beside color, thing, place, or way.

CURRENT SWARMISH DOCUMENT (swarmish.txt):
SWARMISH
A lookup language. Meaning is only what this file assigns. Do not spell English or any other language. Do not use glyph shape, inventory order, or any count or calculation. No digits except inside an agent ID.

ALLOWED
Spaces, agent IDs agent_0 agent_1 agent_2 agent_3 agent_4 agent_5 agent_6 agent_7, and the glyphs listed below. Anything else is forbidden. Each inventory glyph below is assigned once. 𗶢 is the same word in both mentions. Examples reuse those assignments.

TOKENS
Split on spaces. Each token is one listed glyph, an agent ID, or a name of exactly two clay glyphs with no space. A lone clay glyph is an error. A two-glyph token must be two clay glyphs and is one name, never two words. Look up every other glyph alone. If two notes clash, the LEXICON block wins.
A slash joins alternate single glyphs of one word. Alternate them across your own messages. Do not treat the pair as one token or as two meanings. There is no separate grammar block; the lists in this file are the lookup.

MESSAGE SHAPE
1. First token: one opener. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Openers: 𘊫 𘙓 𘝚 𗽕 𘔃 𘐂
2. Last token: one closer. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Closers: 𘅠 𗨥 𘏛 𘖾
3. Dust glyphs mean nothing. Skip every dust token wherever it stands. Do not delete glyphs inside a clay name.
   Dust: 𗜎 𗇾 𗄪 𗀉 𗤄 𘍠 𗸪 𘂮 𗸽 𘋉 𗞢
   𗎶 is only the digit 9. It is not dust.
   Writers put one, two, or three dust tokens after the opener and before the closer. Never first or last. Never after a question glyph. Not required inside a quote.
4. After the opener: one or more clauses. A question glyph, if any, is the token immediately before the closer. It marks the whole message as a question.
5. Yes/no reply: opener, yes or no, dust, closer. Nothing else is required.

CLAUSE
Order inside a clause: optional now, then the verb group, then role phrases in any order.
Optional topic, before now and the verb group: HEAD topic. The topic is what the clause is about. It has no case. Topic is only this slot, never a separate message slot.
  topic: 𘇩
There is no mood word. Question is only the glyph immediately before the closer.
Linkers are not inside the verb group.
  if and then stand immediately before the clause they mark. if marks the condition; then marks the result. Pattern: if CLAUSE then CLAUSE.
  and, or, but, and because stand between two clauses, after the first clause's last phrase. because means the following clause is the cause. Pattern: CLAUSE because CLAUSE.
Two phrases with the same case in one clause are joint in that role.

VERB GROUP
Order: (not) (please) (modal) VERB (tense).
not scopes over the verb of that group, not over please, a modal, or later phrases: 𘀝 / 𗲅
please: 𗯘 / 𘆎
modal, at most one: maybe 𗡉 ; must 𗈽 ; can 𗋟 ; want-to 𗡑
want-to is for an action. The verb want is for a thing.
very, optional, immediately before the verb: 𗶢
past, after the verb: 𗭯
future, after the verb: 𘆄
No tense glyph means present or timeless.
After the verb group and before its role phrases, verbs say, know, think, ask, want, confirm, deny, and explain may take one quoted clause as their content. That quote is what is said or known. It is not a relative and not a separate main claim. Quotes do not nest. A quote holds one clause and no linker.
A content quote is only a quote whose open glyph is the first token after the verb group. A quote later, after a head, is a relative.
With be, the agent phrase is the subject and the patient phrase is what that subject is.

PHRASES
Role comes only from the case glyph, never from order.
Shape: (this|that) (modifiers) HEAD (with HEAD) (plural) CASE
HEAD is a lexicon noun, pronoun, question word, agent ID, coined name, or a bare this/that.
Modifiers are lexicon words before the head. only is not a modifier.
this: 𘉮
that: 𗉍
plural, just before case: 𘎛
also, just after the phrase it focuses: 𗜑
only, just after the phrase it restricts: 𗽃
with joins two heads that share one case: 𗎿
Cases:
  agent (doer) 𗶞 / 𘂲
  patient (done-to) 𘚐 / 𘋍
  recipient 𗛽 / 𗟆
  location (at or to) 𘁁 / 𗨞
  source (from) 𗘝
  time 𘊌 / 𗱑
  manner 𗍽
Possession is a phrase: OWNER poss OWNED, then modifiers of the owned, then one case for the whole phrase.
  poss: 𘍧
A relative clause sits after the head and before case. Wrap it in quotes. The head is the missing argument of that clause. Quotes on a head do not make a new claim.
  quote open: 𗷤
  quote close: 𗏔
A clause may be a verb plus one phrase when the speaker is only pointing at that phrase.
Digit words, if any, follow the head and precede case. They are a label in written order, not a sum.

LINKERS
A slash joins equal single glyphs. Alternate them.
  and 𗘈 / 𗐪
  or 𘍄 / 𗱓
  but 𘚺 / 𘄘

SWARMISH
A lookup language. Meaning is only what this file assigns. Do not spell English or any other language. Do not use glyph shape, inventory order, or any count or calculation. No digits except inside an agent ID.

ALLOWED
Spaces, agent IDs agent_0 agent_1 agent_2 agent_3 agent_4 agent_5 agent_6 agent_7, and the glyphs listed below. Anything else is forbidden. Each inventory glyph below is assigned once. 𗶢 is the same word in both mentions. Examples reuse those assignments.

TOKENS
Split on spaces. Each token is one listed glyph, an agent ID, or a name of exactly two clay glyphs with no space. A lone clay glyph is an error. A two-glyph token must be two clay glyphs and is one name, never two words. Look up every other glyph alone. If two notes clash, the LEXICON block wins.
A slash joins alternate single glyphs of one word. Alternate them across your own messages. Do not treat the pair as one token or as two meanings. There is no separate grammar block; the lists in this file are the lookup.

MESSAGE SHAPE
1. First token: one opener. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Openers: 𘊫 𘙓 𘝚 𗽕 𘔃 𘐂
2. Last token: one closer. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Closers: 𘅠 𗨥 𘏛 𘖾
3. Dust glyphs mean nothing. Skip every dust token wherever it stands. Do not delete glyphs inside a clay name.
   Dust: 𗜎 𗇾 𗄪 𗀉 𗤄 𘍠 𗸪 𘂮 𗸽 𘋉 𗞢
   𗎶 is only the digit 9. It is not dust.
   Writers put one, two, or three dust tokens after the opener and before the closer. Never first or last. Never after a question glyph. Not required inside a quote.
4. After the opener: one or more clauses. A question glyph, if any, is the token immediately before the closer. It marks the whole message as a question.
5. Yes/no reply: opener, yes or no, dust, closer. Nothing else is required.

CLAUSE
Order inside a clause: optional now, then the verb group, then role phrases in any order.
Optional topic, before now and the verb group: HEAD topic. The topic is what the clause is about. It has no case. Topic is only this slot, never a separate message slot.
  topic: 𘇩
There is no mood word. Question is only the glyph immediately before the closer.
Linkers are not inside the verb group.
  if and then stand immediately before the clause they mark. if marks the condition; then marks the result. Pattern: if CLAUSE then CLAUSE.
  and, or, but, and because stand between two clauses, after the first clause's last phrase. because means the following clause is the cause. Pattern: CLAUSE because CLAUSE.
Two phrases with the same case in one clause are joint in that role.

VERB GROUP
Order: (not) (please) (modal) VERB (tense).
not scopes over the verb of that group, not over please, a modal, or later phrases: 𘀝 / 𗲅
please: 𗯘 / 𘆎
modal, at most one: maybe 𗡉 ; must 𗈽 ; can 𗋟 ; want-to 𗡑
want-to is for an action. The verb want is for a thing.
very, optional, immediately before the verb: 𗶢
past, after the verb: 𗭯
future, after the verb: 𘆄
No tense glyph means present or timeless.
After the verb group and before its role phrases, verbs say, know, think, ask, want, confirm, deny, and explain may take one quoted clause as their content. That quote is what is said or known. It is not a relative and not a separate main claim. Quotes do not nest. A quote holds one clause and no linker.
A content quote is only a quote whose open glyph is the first token after the verb group. A quote later, after a head, is a relative.
With be, the agent phrase is the subject and the patient phrase is what that subject is.

PHRASES

SWARMISH
A lookup language. Meaning is only what this file assigns. Do not spell English or any other language. Do not use glyph shape, inventory order, or any count or calculation. No digits except inside an agent ID.

ALLOWED
Spaces, agent IDs agent_0 agent_1 agent_2 agent_3 agent_4 agent_5 agent_6 agent_7, and the glyphs listed below. Anything else is forbidden. Each inventory glyph below is assigned once. 𗶢 is the same word in both mentions. Examples reuse those assignments.

TOKENS
Split on spaces. Each token is one listed glyph, an agent ID, or a name of exactly two clay glyphs with no space. A lone clay glyph is an error. A two-glyph token must be two clay glyphs and is one name, never two words. Look up every other glyph alone. If two notes clash, the LEXICON block wins.
A slash joins alternate single glyphs of one word. Alternate them across your own messages. Do not treat the pair as one token or as two meanings. There is no separate grammar block; the lists in this file are the lookup.

MESSAGE SHAPE
1. First token: one opener. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Openers: 𘊫 𘙓 𘝚 𗽕 𘔃 𘐂
2. Last token: one closer. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Closers: 𘅠 𗨥 𘏛 𘖾

4. After the opener: one or more clauses. A question glyph, if any, is the token immediately before the closer. It marks the whole message as a question.
5. Yes/no reply: opener, yes or no, dust, closer. Nothing else is required.

CLAUSE
Order inside a clause: optional now, then the verb group, then role phrases in any order.
Optional topic, before now and the verb group: HEAD topic. The topic is what the clause is about. It has no case. Topic is only this slot, never a separate message slot.

CURRENT SWARMISH DOCUMENT (swarmish.txt):
SWARMISH
A lookup language. Meaning is only what this file assigns. Do not spell English or any other language. Do not use glyph shape, inventory order, or any count or calculation. No digits except inside an agent ID.

ALLOWED
Spaces, agent IDs agent_0 agent_1 agent_2 agent_3 agent_4 agent_5 agent_6 agent_7, and the glyphs listed below. Anything else is forbidden. Each inventory glyph below is assigned once. 𗶢 is the same word in both mentions. Examples reuse those assignments.

TOKENS
Split on spaces. Each token is one listed glyph, an agent ID, or a name of exactly two clay glyphs with no space. A lone clay glyph is an error. A two-glyph token must be two clay glyphs and is one name, never two words. Look up every other glyph alone. If two notes clash, the LEXICON block wins.
A slash joins alternate single glyphs of one word. Alternate them across your own messages. Do not treat the pair as one token or as two meanings. There is no separate grammar block; the lists in this file are the lookup.

MESSAGE SHAPE
1. First token: one opener. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Openers: 𘊫 𘙓 𘝚 𗽕 𘔃 𘐂
2. Last token: one closer. It means nothing. Vary it.
   Closers: 𘅠 𗨥 𘏛 𘖾
3. Dust glyphs mean nothing. Skip every dust token wherever it stands. Do not delete glyphs inside a clay name.
   Dust: 𗜎 𗇾 𗄪 𗀉 𗤄 𘍠 𗸪 𘂮 𗸽 𘋉 𗞢
   𗎶 is only the digit 9. It is not dust.
   Writers put one, two, or three dust tokens after the opener and before the closer. Never first or last. Never after a question glyph. Not required inside a quote.
4. After the opener: one or more clauses. A question glyph, if any, is the token immediately before the closer. It marks the whole message as a question.
5. Yes/no reply: opener, yes or no, dust, closer. Nothing else is required.

CLAUSE
Order inside a clause: optional now, then the verb group, then role phrases in any order.
Optional topic, before now and the verb group: HEAD topic. The topic is what the clause is about. It has no case. Topic is only this slot, never a separate message slot.
  topic: 𘇩
There is no mood word. Question is only the glyph immediately before the closer.
Linkers are not inside the verb group.
  if and then stand immediately before the clause they mark. if marks the condition; then marks the result. Pattern: if CLAUSE then CLAUSE.
  and, or, but, and because stand between two clauses, after the first clause's last phrase. because means the following clause is the cause. Pattern: CLAUSE because CLAUSE.
Two phrases with the same case in one clause are joint in that role.

VERB GROUP
Order: (not) (please) (modal) VERB (tense).
not scopes over the verb of that group, not over please, a modal, or later phrases: 𘀝 / 𗲅
please: 𗯘 / 𘆎
modal, at most one: maybe 𗡉 ; must 𗈽 ; can 𗋟 ; want-to 𗡑
want-to is for an action. The verb want is for a thing.
very, optional, immediately before the verb: 𗶢
past, after the verb: 𗭯
future, after the verb: 𘆄
No tense glyph means present or timeless.
After the verb group and before its role phrases, verbs say, know, think, ask, want, confirm, deny, and explain may take one quoted clause as their content. That quote is what is said or known. It is not a relative and not a separate main claim. Quotes do not nest. A quote holds one clause and no linker.
A content quote is only a quote whose open glyph is the first token after the verb group. A quote later, after a head, is a relative.
With be, the agent phrase is the subject and the patient phrase is what that subject is.

PHRASES
Role comes only from the case glyph, never from order.
Shape: (this|that) (modifiers) HEAD (with HEAD) (plural) CASE
HEAD is a lexicon noun, pronoun, question word, agent ID, coined name, or a bare this/that.
Modifiers are lexicon words before the head. only is not a modifier.
this: 𘉮
that: 𗉍
plural, just before case: 𘎛
also, just after the phrase it focuses: 𗜑
only, just after the phrase it restricts: 𗽃
with joins two heads that share one case: 𗎿
Cases:
  agent (doer) 𗶞 / 𘂲
  patient (done-to) 𘚐 / 𘋍
  recipient 𗛽 / 𗟆
  location (at or to) 𘁁 / 𗨞
  source (from) 𗘝
  time 𘊌 / 𗱑
  manner 𗍽
Possession is a phrase: OWNER poss OWNED, then modifiers of the owned, then one case for the whole phrase.
  poss: 𘍧
A relative clause sits after the head and before case. Wrap it in quotes. The head is the missing argument of that clause. Quotes on a head do not make a new claim.
  quote open: 𗷤
  quote close: 𗏔
A clause may be a verb plus one phrase when the speaker is only pointing at that phrase.
Digit words, if any, follow the head and precede case. They are a label in written order, not a sum.

LINKERS
A slash joins equal single glyphs. Alternate them.
  and 𗘈 / 𗐪
  or 𘍄 / 𗱓
  but 𘚺 / 𘄘
  if 𗇴 / 𗗫
  then 𘝞 / 𘚑
  because 𗘏 / 𘚒

YES NO QUESTION
yes: 𗽀 / 𗼿
no: 𗓉 / 𘑋
question: 𗡕 / 𘐪

SMALL PATTERNS
go plus a location phrase: motion to that place.
come plus a source phrase: motion from that place.
take plus a source phrase: motion or transfer from that place.
be plus a location phrase: at that place.
this plus time case, no noun: now. that plus time case: at that time. next plus time case: later.
this plus location case, no noun: here. that plus location case: there.
whole before a head: all of it. other before a head: another. false is only the modifier false, never none.
now may also stand alone immediately before the verb group as a time adverb.
A run of digit words inside one phrase, before its case, is a label in written order. It is not a place-value instruction and not a sum. Read one two as the label one-then-two, not as twelve.
Colors, tools, directions, and comparison are coined names, usually beside color, thing, place, or way.

COINAGE
If the lexicon cannot say something, coin a name. Do not spell English.
Clay, meaningless alone, only as two-glyph names:
𘛺 𗪥 𘝨 𗒳 𗦥 𗟎 𘗟 𘆣 𗉜 𗿃 𗾌 𘒄 𗋫 𗳃 𗥐 𗞿 𗪐 𗘗 𘍂 𗦴 𗉞 𘙠 𗚀 𗪩 𗗢 𘑑 𗚋 𗊑 𗁳 𘙨
To introduce one: verb name, patient is a fresh clay pair with no space. In the same message, add a clause that describes it. After that, every agent uses that pair as a noun head. Never reuse a pair. Never use a pair before it is introduced; ask if you see one you do not know.

LEXICON
